articles.title: Binance Hack May Involve Key Misuse, Not Theft: Blockaid
articles.text:
Binance hack may involve private key ‘misuse,’ not theft: Blockaid CEO
Blockaid’s Ido Ben-Natan suspects attackers manipulated Binance’s transaction-signing infrastructure, drawing parallels with the Bybit hack.
The suspected multi-billion-dollar Binance hack may have involved attackers manipulating the exchange’s transaction-signing signature rather than stealing private keys, according to Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan.
Speaking to Cointelegraph, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key.
“It seems to be… a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.
Ben-Natan said this was a preliminary assessment, drawing on their experience with similar attacks and their observations of the onchain activity.
Binance has not confirmed the precise method that allowed hackers to steal over $2.5 billion in crypto from the exchange — the largest crypto hack in history.
Arkham CEO Miguel Morel told Cointelegraph there isn’t enough information at this point in time to confirm whether the attack involved stolen keys or compromised infrastructure.
“From what we can tell, it appears the hack is still ongoing,” he said.
Related: Binance hack rattles crypto markets as BNB falls 7%, Bitcoin slides
Blockaid identifies malicious wallet delegation
In its onchain analysis published on X, Blockaid said the attacker bundled 50 EIP-7702 authorizations into a single transaction targeting Binance 14. One authorization reportedly matched the account’s required nonce, allowing it to be accepted.
EIP-7702 allows an account to delegate execution to smart-contract code. Blockaid said the affected account was delegated to an unverified sweeper contract that allowed a designated operator to drain tokens and Ether.
Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph the operation could have involved multiple compromised devices and movement through the exchange’s network, though this remains unconfirmed.
North Korea, Bybit comparison
Asked whether the suspected signing manipulation resembled the February 2025 Bybit attack, Ben-Natan described the incidents as “very, very similar.”
In that case, Bybit’s published forensic update said attackers compromised a Safe developer’s credentials, accessed the wallet provider’s infrastructure and deceived signers into approving a malicious transaction.
Like Bybit, Ben-Natan said the activity resembled operations linked to North Korean cyber attackers, based on the sophistication of the on-chain preparations.

articles.title: Crypto Market Tanks Amid Binance Hack
articles.text:
Binance hack rattles markets as BNB falls 8%, Bitcoin nears $77K
Bitcoin, Ether and the broader crypto market took a dive as Binance suffered a multibillion-dollar hack.
Update, Oct. 30 at 1:19 am UTC: This article has been updated with fresh market data, Binance’s pledge to cover all losses and its revised frozen assets total.
Cryptocurrency markets extended their decline early Friday following the Binance hack, with BNB down more than 8% over 24 hours and Bitcoin trading near $77,000.
BNB, the native token of BNB Chain, traded near $693, down around 8.2%, according to CoinGecko data at the time of writing. Bitcoin fell 4.8% to about $77,131, while Ether declined 5.7% to about $2,217.
Binance pledged to cover all losses from the hack and suspended all deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks. In a subsequent update, the exchange put the verified total of frozen assets at around $3 billion, up from its earlier figure of $2.54 billion.
Decentralized finance tokens also declined. Aave’s AAVE fell 11.3% to $118.54, while Uniswap’s UNI dropped 10.4% to $6.48, according to CoinGecko.
Aave said it had frozen new deposits and borrowing across its community-operated V3 and V4 markets as a precaution. The lending platform said its contracts were unaffected and users could still withdraw funds and repay loans.
Bitcoin traded below $77,000 as BNB fell 8% over 24 hours. Source: CoinGecko

articles.title: Tampered Ledger Reported In Singapore A Month Before News Broke: Asia Express
articles.text:
Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express
Singapore police say tampered Ledgers started showing up there on September 10. South Korean lawmakers look set to delay the crypto tax law for a fourth time.
Tampered Ledger wallets cost Singapore users $2.7M: Police
Singapore police say at least two cases involving tampered Ledger hardware wallets have been reported since Sept. 10, with combined losses of about 3.5 million Singapore dollars ($2.7 million). It places the first local report almost a month before the wider incident became public.
It’s not clear from the October 28 consumer alert if the September 10 case was reported to police at the time, or was made retrospectively. If the report was timely, it raises questions as to whether Ledger was informed, or if the Singapore Police Force was in a position to issue a public warning earlier. However, the October 28 advisory suggested the police investigation was still in the preliminary stages.
Ledger issued a public alert about tampered Ledgers being found in the CryptoBilis supply chain on October 9. Almost $100 million was drained from wallets containing spyware components.
On Oct. 13, Ledger said it has asked retailers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Hong Kong to suspend sales of Ledger devices as investigations are ongoing.
Singapore police issue tampered Ledgers warning three weeks after the story broke. Source: Singapore Police
Malaysia, Thailand join Singapore’s cross-border stablecoin push
Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank of Thailand joined Singapore’s BLOOM initiative on Friday as policymaker members.
BLOOM, short for Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online, Multi-currency, is a public-private initiative that intends to help financial institutions use stablecoins and tokenized deposits for cross-border payments. It was launched by the Monetary Authority of Singapore in October last year and counts Airwallex, Mastercard, Ripple, Visa and the World Bank Group as members.
DBS survey finds lots of corporate interest in tokenized money
A survey by Singapore bank DBS found that almost 90% of 422 global businesses surveyed are either adopting, or are interested in adopting, tokenized cash to accelerate payments.
SOUTH KOREA
Groundhog Day as Korean lawmakers consider fourth delay of crypto tax
Government officials in South Korea are reportedly weighing another delay of the country’s cryptocurrency tax policy, currently scheduled to be implemented in January 2027.
According to a Monday report from South Korean news outlet Newsis, the crypto income tax could be pushed to 2029 in part because it’s the earliest that officials will be able to share information on taxes related to digital asset exchanges with the US.
The policy, which would impose a 22% tax on crypto gains for investors earning more than 2.5 million Korean won ($1,883) annually.
Bithumb and two other firms report data breaches
Bithumb said its in-house mobile system was hacked and personal information leaked. Brokerage Daishin Securities reported roughly 38,000 customer records exposed and asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments confirmed a hacking incident.
South Korea to regulate stablecoins as payment means, and require monthly balance reporting for cross border transfers
The South Korean government and the Bank of Korea intend to draft amendments to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act within this year to regulate stablecoins used as payment instruments. The central bank will also require crypto transfer service providers to send monthly reports from December 2 — but extending back to mid 2024 — about who exactly has been sending money out of the country.
NORTH KOREA
Chainalysis traces North Korean crypto cash-outs through Garantex
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis mapped a long-running network of Russian intermediaries that helped North Korean IT workers cash out millions of dollars in cryptocurrency.
The US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity on Wednesday for supporting North Korean government-run IT worker schemes that it said funded the country’s weapons programs, according to a press release.
Those sanctioned included Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas.
HONG KONG
Hong Kong names Nasdaq-listed Solana Company a strategic enterprise
Hong Kong has named Nasdaq-listed Solana Company (HSDT) a strategic enterprise under a government program aimed at attracting businesses that support the city’s economic development.
Solana Company said Thursday that it was among the seventh batch of businesses selected by Hong Kong’s Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (OASES) and the only blockchain infrastructure company onboarded by the office in 2026.
Hong Kong’s government confirmed the addition of 18 enterprises to the program last week, bringing its total to 142.
China uses Hong Kong as a launchpad for the Digital Yuan
The South China Morning Post reported that Beijing wants Hong Kong to help seed international use of the digital yuan.
RedotPay plans a US IPO
Hong Kong crypto payments firm RedotPay plans to launch an IPO in the US before the end of the year, and has launched a pre-IPO funding round valuing the company at $4 billion.
CHINA
China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout
China has set a 2030 target for largely completing a national blockchain network under a five-year digital development plan published Friday.
The new plan also calls for stronger blockchain technical standards and greater use of the technology in data circulation and trading.
Mainland China bans cryptocurrency-related business activities, but promotes blockchain technology as a national priority. Critics say that blockchain-not-crypto has never worked before.
THAILAND
Supreme Court recognizes Bitcoin as legal property
Thailand’s Supreme Court has ruled that Bitcoin qualifies as property under criminal law, setting a precedent that may influence how Thai courts treat other cryptocurrencies. The case involved upholding a 10-year prison sentence in a robbery case involving about $50,000 in Bitcoin.
Thailand launches crypto wallet for tourists
Thailand has launched the terribly named WORPT digital wallet so that tourists can convert USDT or USDC into Thai baht in order to spend via PromptPay QR codes. The scheme is part of the Tourist DigiPay sandbox.

articles.title: Live Updates: Binance hit by largest crypto hack in history
articles.text:
Live updates: Binance says $3B in crypto frozen in connection to hack
Follow live updates as Binance says $2.54 billion in assets has been frozen after a multibillion-dollar hack, with further freezes possible as investigators trace funds.
What we know about the Binance hack:
- Binance says the verified total frozen is $2.54 billion and could increase as investigators trace additional assets.
- Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals and deposits as it investigates the security breach.
- An Arkham Intelligence tracker showed about $5.84 billion in assets across wallets linked to the hack. The final loss remains undetermined.
- Circle, Tether, Ripple, World Liberty Financial and Arbitrum have helped to freeze millions in stablecoins.
- The incident did not impact Binance.US.
Oct. 30 at 12:52 am UTC
Binance says $3 billion now frozen from hack
Binance said the current verified amount of assets frozen from the hack is now $3 billion.
The update came after the Arbitrum Security Council said it executed a transaction to freeze $30.5 million from the Binance exploit, involving 74.6 million Arbitrum (ARB) and 8,425 Ether (ETH).
“The Security Council acted by weighing its commitment to the security and integrity of the Arbitrum community and Arbitrum governance without impacting any Arbitrum users or applications,” it said.
“As of October 30, 2026 time, the funds have been successfully transferred to an intermediary frozen wallet,” it said.
The funds will no longer be accessible to the address that originally held the funds and can only be moved by further action of the Security Council or a vote of Arbitrum DAO governance, it added.
Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC
Chainalysis estimates $5.9 billion stolen from Binance
Chainalysis said its current estimate of the amount stolen from Binance is $5.912 billion at the time of theft, four times the amount stolen from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
Binance earlier said the verified total frozen is $2.54 billion.
Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC
Blockaid suspects Binance hack involved private key ‘misuse,’ not theft
The suspected multi-billion-dollar Binance hack may have involved attackers manipulating the exchange’s transaction-signing signature rather than stealing private keys, according to Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan.
Speaking to Cointelegraph, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key.
“It seems to be… a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.
Ben-Natan said this was a preliminary assessment, drawing on their experience with similar attacks and their observations of the onchain activity.
Arkham CEO Miguel Morel said the attack appears to be ongoing.
Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC
Binance says deposits temporarily suspended
Binance said it has temporarily suspended deposits as it conducts security checks, freezes funds and coordinates with law enforcement. It previously confirmed it had suspended withdrawals.
“We are working around the clock and will share a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete,” the company said, adding it will “cover all losses.”
Earlier, Binance also said it had temporarily suspended Binance Alpha trading.
Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC
Wintermute and GSR disclose Binance exposure
Crypto trading firms Wintermute and GSR disclosed exposure to Binance but said they did not expect major disruption to their businesses.
The firms are market makers, which place buy and sell orders on exchanges to help other traders complete transactions. A disruption to their operations could make trading harder or more expensive across crypto markets.
GSR CEO Xin Song said its Binance exposure was less than 5% of its net equity, meaning the value of its assets minus its liabilities. He said GSR was working with Binance to understand the incident and identify ways to help.
Wintermute CEO Evgeny Gaevoy said his firm’s exposure was less than 20% of net equity and that he did not expect operational disruption.
Neither executive disclosed a dollar amount for the exposure or confirmed financial losses.
Oct. 29 at 11:40 pm UTC
Ripple freezes RLUSD linked to Binance hack
Ripple is freezing holdings of its dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin linked to the Binance hack, according to Jack McDonald, the company’s senior vice president of stablecoins.
McDonald said Ripple was “actively freezing affected funds” and coordinating with relevant parties to support the investigation. He did not disclose the amount frozen.
Oct. 29 at 11:35 pm UTC
Binance says $2.54 billion frozen after hack
Binance said the verified total of assets frozen in connection with the hack had reached $2.54 billion, clarifying differing figures circulating publicly, including references to $1.8 billion.
The exchange said the total could increase as its teams work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets. Binance said it would publish further figures once verified.
Oct. 29 at 10:36 pm UTC
World Liberty Financial freezes $27 million in USD1
World Liberty Financial has frozen $27 million in US-dollar-pegged stablecoin USD1 and $2 million worth of WLFI, according to Binance co-founder Yi He.
“USD1 has taken proactive steps to freeze the $27 million in USD1 associated with the Binance hack,” said World Liberty Financial co-founder and CEO Zach Witkoff.
World Liberty Financial said it worked with BitGo to freeze the stolen WLFI and USD1 funds.
“We will cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation and support efforts to hold those responsible accountable. Protecting our users remains a top priority,” said World Liberty in a post on X.
Oct. 29 at 10:33 pm UTC
Binance says withdrawals will resume once issues resolved
Binance says its team is conducting security checks and will resume withdrawals as soon as the “security issue” is resolved.
Oct. 29 at 10:32 pm UTC
Aave freezes markets after Binance exploiter borrows $44.6 million
Decentralized lending protocol Aave froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments as a precaution following the Binance hack.
In a governance forum update posted after the freeze, risk service provider LlamaRisk said the Binance exploiter deposited 60 million USDT and borrowed 19,762 Wrapped Ether (WETH), worth about $44.6 million at the time.
The borrowing occurred between 8:58 pm and 9:01 pm UTC on Oct. 29, about 40 minutes before the first freeze. It was the exploiter’s only Aave position across all networks and versions, with no further interactions detected after 9:01 pm UTC.
The position remained backed by $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt at the update’s snapshot. LlamaRisk said it remained subject to normal liquidation and did not put Aave suppliers at risk.
The freezes covered 175 reserves on V3 across 16 networks and 117 reserves on V4 across four networks.
Users can still withdraw funds and repay loans, and liquidations continue. However, the freeze prevents new deposits and borrowing, including additional collateral deposits, leaving repayment as the only way to improve an existing position’s health factor.
LlamaRisk said markets would remain frozen until the exploiter’s funds stopped moving and Binance provided greater clarity on containment, followed by a staged reopening. It warned that a prolonged freeze could push borrowing rates higher as withdrawals reduce available liquidity.
Oct. 29 at 9:19 pm UTC
Binance investigates $5.8 billion security breach
Binance is investigating a potential multibillion-dollar security breach involving one of its Ethereum wallets, after suspicious transfers prompted stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle to reportedly freeze billions in assets.
A Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph on Thursday that the exchange was investigating reports of a potential security issue but had not confirmed any impact on user funds. The spokesperson said its security teams were reviewing the activity and would provide updates once more information was verified.
Concerns were first raised by blockchain researcher Spreek, who posted on X that assets from a Binance-linked Ethereum wallet had been transferred to a newly created address through a contract call allegedly funded by Tornado Cash. Spreek later reported that wallets connected to the transfers had begun selling Tether USDt (USDT) through decentralized exchanges.
Blockchain analytics platform Arkham Intelligence later identified a collection of wallets labeled “binance-hacker-1029” holding approximately $5.84 billion in digital assets. The figure represents the wallets’ reported holdings rather than a confirmed estimate of stolen funds.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the activity appeared to be a hack, adding that Tether and Circle had frozen approximately $971 million and $823 million, respectively. Zhao said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.
Source: Arkham Intelligence
Tether, Circle freeze over $2.36 billion as Binance outflows reach $3.3 billion
Blockchain security firm Blockaid said its team had identified roughly $3.3 billion in suspicious transfers involving Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Avalanche.
Shortly after news of the hack emerged, Tether and Circle, the two largest stablecoin issuers by market capitalization, said they had frozen a combined $2.36 billion in tokens linked to the suspected incident.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement and would continue supporting the investigation.
A few minutes later, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.567 billion in USDT linked to the potential exploit.
“Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority,” Ardoino wrote.
The Binance hack came hours after Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a compromise at a third-party provider. The prediction market platform said it had fixed the issue and pledged to reimburse affected users, with all systems reported operational by 7:05 p.m. UTC Thursday.

articles.title: Crypto Today: Kalshi Raises $1B, HTX UK Settlement, AI Agents
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, prediction market platform Kalshi raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation, cryptocurrency exchange HTX agreed to halt unlawful promotions in the UK following legal action by the Financial Conduct Authority and CFTC Chair Michael Selig outlined a future where AI-powered refrigerators could stake Ether and launch memecoins.
Kalshi hits $40 billion valuation after $1 billion funding round
Prediction market platform Kalshi has raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation, nearly doubling since May as it expands beyond sports contracts.
Wellington Management and Sequoia Capital co-led the Series G round, Reuters reported Thursday. Kalshi also disclosed that its non-sports markets have surpassed $1 billion in annualized revenue, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The latest financing follows a $1 billion raise in May that valued Kalshi at $22 billion. The platform has since recorded approximately $15.8 billion in trading volume over the past 30 days, according to DefiLlama.
Kalshi is also expanding its commercial partnerships. Earlier this week, the NBA named Kalshi and rival Polymarket as preferred prediction market exchanges, while S&P Dow Jones Indices partnered with Kalshi to introduce financial benchmarks to event contracts.
The expansion comes amid mounting legal scrutiny of Kalshi’s sports contracts. Utah filed criminal charges against the company and its co-founders Wednesday over alleged illegal gambling activities, escalating a dispute over whether prediction markets fall under federal derivatives oversight or state gambling laws. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has separately moved to block Utah’s enforcement efforts.
HTX agrees to halt unlawful UK crypto promotions after FCA case
Cryptocurrency exchange HTX has agreed to stop unlawfully promoting its services to consumers in the United Kingdom under a settlement announced Thursday by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
Huobi Global S.A., the Panamanian company behind HTX, agreed that it would not knowingly run illegal promotions, including through the exchange’s website, apps or social media. The court undertakings run until Oct. 21, 2031.
The settlement terms are confidential, and the agreement does not constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing.
“Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law,” said Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA. “The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences.”
In an Oct. 16 notice outlining its UK exit arrangements, the exchange formerly known as Huobi said existing UK accounts could no longer deposit or trade. Eligible users can request a one-time 48-hour window to withdraw remaining assets, subject to approval and compliance checks. Accounts will close after all assets have been withdrawn.
The FCA brought the case in October 2025 and announced it in February, which it said was the agency’s first enforcement action against a crypto firm over illegal marketing.
Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins: CFTC chair
Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chair Michael Selig says it is “no longer science fiction” to imagine one’s refrigerator autonomously purchasing groceries with money earned from staking Ether — or even launching its own memecoin, raising questions about how regulators should oversee autonomous AI agents.
The colorful comment came during Selig’s remarks at the CFTC’s inaugural Frontier Forum in Washington, DC, on Wednesday, where he argued that regulators must adapt to a financial system where AI agents can hold assets and execute trades autonomously.
“We’re gathered here today to discuss a technology that’s rapidly transforming the financial markets. President Trump calls it ‘super intelligence,’ or SI, because ‘it’s not artificial.’ It’s as real as the printing press, the steam engine, and the internet,” he said.
The regulatory questions come as younger investors embrace AI tools for managing money. An eToro survey published in September found that 79% of US millennial investors and 77% of Gen Z investors already used or were open to using AI to select or adjust their investments, highlighting the potential reach of rules governing automated finance.

articles.title: Blockchain industry revenue shifts toward publicly traded firms
articles.text:
Public companies double share of blockchain revenue since 2022: Report
A new 1kx report finds that public companies are capturing a larger share of blockchain revenue, driven by institutional adoption and real-world applications.
Publicly traded companies accounted for 16% of blockchain industry revenue in 2026, more than double their 7% share in 2022, according to a new report from crypto investment firm 1kx.
The increase comes as overall blockchain revenue is projected to decline 28% year over year to roughly $100 billion in 2026. The report analyzed data from more than 2,600 protocols and earnings reports from 104 publicly traded companies through the third quarter.
The researchers attributed the growing share of public companies partly to new stock market listings, including stablecoin issuer Circle, which went public in 2025, and revenue growth among existing companies. The 10 largest publicly traded companies in the study doubled their blockchain-related revenue over the past three years.
Coinbase and Circle generated approximately $3.3 billion in combined blockchain-related revenue in the first half of 2026, according to 1kx, while publicly traded Bitcoin miners earned roughly $2 billion. Traditional financial firms, including JPMorgan, BlackRock, CME Group, Visa and Robinhood, accounted for another $1.1 billion collectively.
Revenue remains concentrated among a relatively small number of businesses. The six largest publicly traded companies accounted for roughly 50% to 60% of the group’s revenue, according to the report.
Related: BlackRock files for third Bitcoin ETF, still no Solana or XRP
Institutional and real-world activity gains share of blockchain revenue
The report also found that revenue from broader economic activity surpassed blockchain infrastructure revenue for the first time in the third quarter, reaching approximately $5.3 billion compared with $5.1 billion, according to 1kx.
The category, which includes tokenized assets, payments and prediction markets, grew 58% year over year in the first half of 2026. Together with institutional adoption, it accounted for 33% of total blockchain revenue in the third quarter, with the report projecting a 30% share for the full year.
Institutional and broader economic activity to reach 30% of blockchain revenue in 2026. Source: 1kx report
RWA.xyz data shows the value of distributed tokenized real-world assets rose roughly 51% over the past year, from $26.16 billion in October 2025 to $39.54 billion as of Thursday. Tokenized equities grew even faster, surging 471% over the same period to $3.77 billion.

articles.title: Polymarket Reported ’Major Outage,’ Suspended Trading
articles.text:
Polymarket suspended trading amid reports of user funds being drained
The prediction markets platform halted trading on Thursday after it reported one of its third party providers had been compromised.
Prediction markets company Polymarket reported its Predictions Trading API had experienced a “major outage,” resulting in the platform temporarily halting trading.
In a Thursday update to its status page, Polymarket said that the platform was in “cancel-only” mode after it had identified and fixed an issue impacting its operations. As of 7:05 pm UTC, the platform reported all its systems were operational.
“One of our third party providers was compromised, and we have referred this to relevant law enforcement,” said Polymarket. “Anyone who has been impacted will be made whole.”
The suspension of trading came as several users claimed online that their Polymarket accounts had been drained of thousands of dollars after their positions were sold without their consent. In June, Polymarket reported that hackers were able to drain more than $2.9 million in user funds by compromising a third-party vendor.
Related: Coinbase denies systems breach, says vendor exposed customer data

articles.title: HYPE Jumps 20% as ICE Plans US Hyperliquid Perpetual Futures
articles.text:
HYPE teases all-time high as NYSE owner ICE eyes US Hyperliquid perps
Hyperliquid’s token pumped following news of ICE and Trade[XYZ] unveiling plans for US perpetual futures.
Hyperliquid’s native token HYPE surged about 20% Thursday after New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) announced plans for US perpetual futures with Trade[XYZ], whose investors include billionaire Wall Street investor Stanley Druckenmiller.
HYPE traded above $96 at the time of writing, up by around 20% in the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko, flirting with September’s all-time record of $97.96.
Perpetual futures allow traders to take positions on asset prices without an expiration date. Hyperliquid is the largest decentralized exchange in the world to trade such instruments, DefiLlama data shows.
The companies said Thursday they would seek regulatory approval for markets covering cryptocurrencies, stocks, indexes, commodities and currencies. The proposed market would target retail traders. ICE said it would operate separately from its institutional futures business, with a dedicated clearing structure.
More than 99% of participation in its markets is institutional, ICE said, with the separate clearing structure intended to shield existing customers from retail counterparty risks.
The proposal would give US retail traders a regulated route to Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures, and ICE a new route into retail trading. President Donald Trump said on Aug. 19 that Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the country in a “fully compliant and legal fashion.”
Related: Wall Street wealth creation model is unsustainable for most participants: Hyperliquid CEO
Druckenmiller investment draws Musk reaction
“I am excited to be an investor in trade(xyz),” Druckenmiller wrote on X, adding that he looked forward to using its products.
Elon Musk also drew attention to the agreement, sharing Druckenmiller’s post with the one-word comment “Interesting.”
ICE is taking a minority stake in Trade[XYZ], but disclosed neither the investment amount nor a launch date. Cointelegraph reached out to ICE and Trade[XYZ] for comment but had not received a response by publication.
Customers would undergo identity and Anti-Money-Laundering checks and trade through participating futures brokers.
Distribution is expected through ICE’s joint venture with OKX, pending separate approvals. ICE invested in OKX at a $25 billion valuation in March.
Related: ICE, CME press US regulators to ‘rein in’ Hyperliquid energy trading: Report
OKX venture faces issuer objections
Meanwhile, ICE’s separate tokenized stock venture with OKX has disclosed objections from 38 companies, up from 26 reported by Cointelegraph on Oct. 27.
Its Oct. 28 notice adds Walmart, Eli Lilly, Carnival, Arcos Dorados and Cigna. However, those objections concern tokenized shares, while the Trade[XYZ] proposal involves perpetual futures and remains subject to separate regulatory approvals.
The regulatory opening remains conditional. The CFTC approved Kalshi’s Bitcoin perpetual contract in May, but said perpetuals referencing other asset classes should receive case-by-case review.
Magazine: HYPE price could suffer as Binance takes its revenue: Alice Liu

articles.title: Binance Hacker Hunts for Exit Ramps as DeFi Exchanges Pause Markets - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Wallets tied to the suspected Binance hack received tens of thousands of ETH from Uniswap contracts and borrowed 19,762 ETH on Aave against about $60 million in USDT, with no sign of a flaw in either app.
- About 253,000 ETH, roughly $570 million, sat in two wallets with no outgoing transfers as of 22:07 UTC, and ETH has no issuer that can freeze it.
- Ripple has frozen about $200 million in RLUSD, per Binance co-CEO Yi He, on top of the more than $2 billion in USDT and USDC.
The attacker behind the wallets draining Binance is using decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap and Aave as exits, swapping stablecoins that issuers can freeze for Ethereum that nobody can, according to Etherscan records for 10 wallets, eight of them labeled as exploiters.
Earlier today, wallets linked to the world’s largest crypto exchange were drained of at least $5.5 billion, with the total tally still climbing. The company said it was investigating the security incident but did not confirm user funds were affected, though security experts widely believe the exchange was indeed hacked. It stands to be the largest hack in the crypto industry's 18-year history.
Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle moved quickly to blacklist the suspected attacker’s addresses in order to freeze a portion of the funds and make them inaccessible. As centralized issuers, they each have the ability to blacklist addresses so their tokens cannot move, and more than $2 billion of those two tokens have been frozen so far by different stablecoin providers. ETH has no issuer, so every dollar converted before a freeze lands is out of their reach.
The swaps run through Uniswap, a decentralized exchange where trades settle automatically with no company in the middle.
One relay wallet received 20,940 ETH ($45.58 Million) from Uniswap’s UniswapX contract at 20:34 UTC, another got 3,552 ETH (over $8 million) at 20:47, and two later wallets took in about 18,085 ETH (around $41 million) from Uniswap contracts, in 7,444 ETH and 10,642 ETH batches, and about 16,498 ETH ($37.5 million), in 6,946 ETH and 9,552 ETH batches.
Aave, a lending app where users deposit crypto as collateral to borrow other coins, offered a second exit. Between 20:57 and 21:01 UTC, one wallet deposited $10 million and then $50 million in USDT and borrowed 3,271 ETH ($7.43 million) and then 16,491 ETH ($37.47 million) against it, which prompted cybersecurity experts Odysseas Lamtzidi, founder of Phylax Systems, to warn of “contagion in full effect.”
Update: https://t.co/G3Z72cuDXM
They just approved AAVE.
Contagion in full effect https://t.co/aNz2snt8E6
— Odysseus | phylax.systems (@odysseas_eth) October 29, 2026
Aave has since frozen its V3 markets on Ethereum mainnet, which blocks new deposits and borrowing.
Kamino, a decentralized finance protocol built on the Solana blockchain, also paused its Solana and Bitcoin markets as a precautionary measure.
Kamino can confirm that it is currently unaffected by the ongoing Binance situation
Out of an abundance of caution, we have temporarily paused borrowing in the SOL/BTC Market
We are actively monitoring the situation and are in communication with various partners. Any further…
— Kamino (@kamino) October 29, 2026
The ETH is piling up rather than moving on. A wallet labeled Exploiter 8 still held 195,460 ETH ($444.2 million) at 22:03 UTC, and another 57,891.77 ETH ($131.6 million) reached one labeled Exploiter 11, together about 253,000 ETH, or roughly $570 million. That second pile arrived after four hops in 28 minutes, from Exploiter 4 to 5, 5 to 6, 6 to 7 and 7 to 11.
The attacker also swapped 36 million RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar-backed stablecoin, for 15,439 ETH, while 52.54 million RLUSD remained unfrozen at the holding wallet, according to an on-chain update circulating on X. Etherscan showed the main receiving wallet holding about $88.5 million in RLUSD at 20:41 UTC, which matches the two figures combined.
Ripple has since frozen about $200 million, according to Binance co-CEO Yi He. “Thanks to the Ripple team for promptly freezing approximately 200 million. User Funds are SAFU,” a reference to the exchange’s emergency reserve fund, Yi He wrote on X.
“Ripple is closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and its attackers’ RLUSD holdings and we are actively freezing affected funds,” Jack McDonald, Ripple’s senior vice president for stablecoins, said in a statement. “We’re coordinating with relevant parties and stand ready to support any investigation and appropriate action to keep users protected.”
Ripple is closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and its attackers’ RLUSD holdings and we are actively freezing affected funds. We’re coordinating with relevant parties and stand ready to support any investigation and appropriate action to keep users…
— Jack McDonald (@_JackMcDonald_) October 29, 2026
Tornado Cash, a mixer that scrambles the trail of crypto payments, appears so far only as funding for the address that set up the attack.
After the Bybit hack, North Korea’s Lazarus Group converted 84.45% of the stolen ETH to Bitcoin through Thorchain, a cross-chain swap network, per Bybit’s CEO. Monero, a privacy coin that hides who sent what, rose about 6% on Thursday, suggesting a possible rotation into the privacy coin.

articles.title: KuCoin To Suspend Services in Russia and Belarus, Citing Compliance
articles.text:
KuCoin suspends services in Russia and Belarus
The exchange cited legal and regulatory compliance in its reason for cutting off services to users based in the two countries, currently the targets of international sanctions.
Cryptocurrency exchange KuCoin announced that it would immediately suspend services for its users in Russia and Belarus, citing legal and regulatory compliance concerns.
In a Thursday notice, KuCoin said it had suspended access to all products and services for users based in Russia and Belarus. According to the exchange, it would offer an “orderly exit process” to allow users to withdraw assets.
“Compliance is at the core of our operations and guides our decisions on where and how we offer our services,” said the exchange in a Thursday X post regarding the service suspension.
The move comes as many crypto companies are complying with international sanctions led by the United States and Europe against Russia and Belarus over the war in Ukraine. KuCoin is headquartered in the Seychelles.
Separately, Russia’s central bank on Thursday approved the National Association of Securities Market Participants, commonly known as NAUFOR, as a self-regulatory body for crypto exchanges and custodians. The central bank’s registry currently includes 23 crypto exchanges and eight digital custody institutions, with registered entities required to join a self-regulatory organization within 90 days.
Related: UK sanctions three crypto exchanges tied to Russian illicit funds

articles.title: Binance Drained of $5.5 Billion in Suspected Hack, Tether and Circle Freeze $1.8 Billion - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- At least $5.57 billion left Binance-linked wallets on Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron on Thursday, per an on-chain tally; Binance said it is investigating.
- Tether froze 975.1 million USDT and Circle froze 823 million USDC in the main receiving wallet, about $1.8 billion in total.
- Bitcoin fell below $79,000, BNB dropped about 7% and Monero rose about 6%.
At least $5.57 billion in crypto has left wallets linked to Binance across three blockchains in what appears to be a breach of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange.
If confirmed as a hack, it would be the biggest crypto hack on record. Binance has not confirmed its exchange has been hacked but said it is aware of the “potential security issue and is actively investigating.”
“We have not confirmed any impact to user funds,” the company posted on X. “Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.”
Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating. At this stage, we have not confirmed any impact to user funds.
Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official… pic.twitter.com/dN76yhzYM0
— Binance (@binance) October 29, 2026
Binance is the world's largest crypto exchange, where millions of people buy, sell and store their coins. The money came from its hot wallets, the internet-connected wallets exchanges use to process customer withdrawals.
The tally counts $3.51 billion on Ethereum, $1.44 billion in 18,270 Bitcoin and $630 million on Tron. The first Ethereum transaction, at 20:24 UTC, sent 167,464 ETH plus 63 token transfers to a brand-new address, including 1.615 billion USDT, a stablecoin built to always trade at $1, according to Etherscan.
Three minutes earlier, an address funded through Tornado Cash, a mixer that scrambles the trail of crypto payments, submitted a delegation for a Binance hot wallet using EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets an ordinary wallet run smart-contract code. “7702 lets a normal wallet execute delegated code. The delegation persists; that code can authorize later transfers without another signature from the wallet,” Odysseas Lamtzidi, founder of Phylax Systems wrote on X.
1/4 EIP-7702 can turn the wallet itself into the sweeper.
A Binance-labeled wallet moved 167,464 ETH + 63 tokens, including 1.615B USDT, just 3m24s after a signed delegation was installed.
This is bad.https://t.co/GrvUiya16D pic.twitter.com/zONu8cwW63
— Odysseus | phylax.systems (@odysseas_eth) October 29, 2026
How the attacker got the required signature is still unknown. Tether froze 975.1 million USDT in the main receiving address, and Circle, issuer of the rival stablecoin USDC, froze 823 million USDC in the same wallet at 21:04 UTC, bringing the total frozen to about $1.8 billion. Both issuers can block specific addresses from moving their tokens, but the attacker is moving funds fast.
"Circle is closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance," Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire posted on X. "In coordination with law enforcement, we have frozen more than 800M USDC associated with the incident and will continue supporting the investigation."
Total on the hack is at least $5.57B across 3 chains (likely more)
Tether has started freezing and this time even Circle acted and managed to freeze 800M in a single wallet.
Total frozen: $1.8B
Still $800M could be frozen, attacker is moving funds fast https://t.co/km4eyJWEa8 pic.twitter.com/IL6wBfZK2r
— Wazz (@WazzCrypto) October 29, 2026
Bitcoin slid below $79,000, down about 2.6% in 24 hours, while BNB, Binance's own token, fell about 7% to roughly $699. Monero, a privacy coin that hides who sent what, rose about 6% to $637, echoing the jump of as much as 51% it posted after a $333 million Bitcoin theft in April 2025.
Binance lost 7,000 Bitcoin, about $40 million, in a 2019 hack. The $5.57 billion tally would be more than triple the roughly $1.5 billion Bybit heist in February 2025, the previous record.

articles.title: Coinbase Swings to $719 Million Q3 Profit on Crypto Gains - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Coinbase posted $719 million in Q3 net income, or $2.51 per share, against an expected loss, though about $715 million came from gains on crypto it holds. Adjusted net income was $78 million.
- Revenue of $1.22 billion was in line with estimates and flat from the prior quarter, down 35% from a year earlier.
- Prediction markets topped $200 million in annualized revenue, and subscription and services revenue reached nearly half of net revenue.
Coinbase is back in the black, though much of that came from the crypto on its own balance sheet.
The exchange reported third-quarter net income of $719 million, or $2.51 per diluted share, on Thursday, ending a two-quarter losing streak. Analysts had expected a loss of 15 cents per share, according to Zacks. But about $715 million of the profit came from gains on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment. Excluding those and other investment gains, adjusted net income was $78 million.
Total revenue came in at $1.22 billion, in line with expectations, flat from the second quarter and down 35% from a year earlier. Transaction revenue slipped 1% to $590 million but beat the roughly $527 million analysts expected, as crypto volatility sank to multiyear lows and trading volume across the market fell.
The standout was prediction markets, which crossed $200 million in annualized revenue, making it one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase’s history, the company said.
Daily traders grew more than 60% from the prior quarter, and revenue has compounded 82% per quarter since launch. CEO Brian Armstrong said the product kept “growing even through slower sports months.”
Subscription and services revenue rose 3% to $570 million, nearly half of net revenue, led by $307 million from stablecoins. Average USDC held in Coinbase products hit a record $22 billion. Paid Coinbase One subscribers reached an all-time high, up 24% from a year earlier, and the exchange’s share of global crypto trading volume rose to 10.7%, its fourth straight quarterly gain.
“Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility,” CFO Alesia Haas said.
Coinbase also cut its 2026 adjusted expense guidance by another $100 million at the midpoint, to between $4.15 billion and $4.3 billion, following cost reductions in May. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 60% from the prior quarter to $333 million. Through Oct. 25, fourth-quarter transaction revenue stood at about $165 million.
The positive results follow two consecutive losing quarters. Coinbase posted a $394 million loss in the first quarter and missed estimates in the second as trading activity slowed, though analysts said at the time they weren’t worried about the stock’s slide.
Shares closed Thursday at $160.59, down 1.1%, before the results came out, and were little changed in after-hours trading. The stock is down more than 55% from its 52-week high of $361.40.

articles.title: Canton Strategic Holdings Plans Tokenized CNTN Stock Trading
articles.text:
Nasdaq-listed Canton Strategic Holdings plans tokenized stock trading from Nov. 2
The tokenized shares would carry the same shareholder rights as traditional stock, with round-the-clock trading and immediate settlement under the SEC’s innovation exemption.
Canton Strategic Holdings, a Nasdaq-listed company formerly known as biotechnology firm Tharimmune, announced plans to tokenize its common shares on the Canton Network, with trading expected to begin as soon as Nov. 2.
According to a Thursday announcement, the company partnered with TSV LLC, a trading venue for tokenized securities, and Fairmint, a US Securities and Exchange Commission-registered transfer agent, to bring its shares onto the blockchain. The tokenized shares would carry the same shareholder rights as the company’s Nasdaq-listed stock.
The Nasdaq-traded issue, under the ticker CNTN, currently trade an average daily volume of 757,704 shares, according to Yahoo Finance data. At last look, the stock was up more than 4.5% on the day, trading at roughly $2.13 apiece, with a market cap of $170 million.
Tokenized share trading would be available around the clock through an automated market maker, with transactions settling immediately on the Canton Network. Fairmint would maintain ownership records and oversee compliance with share transfer requirements.
The announcement follows the SEC’s September innovation exemption, which the companies said provides a regulatory path for trading tokenized US stocks on domestic platforms.
Canton Strategic Holdings shifted its focus to digital assets in November 2025 after raising $545 million to build a business around Canton Coin. It changed its name in February and now holds the cryptocurrency, helps operate the Canton Network, and invests in projects built on the blockchain.
Despite its name, Canton Strategic Holdings is not the company behind the Canton Network, which was developed by Digital Asset. However, it has ties to the Canton Foundation through its investments and participation in network governance.
Related: Crypto’s 2026 shutdown wave claims 82 projects. What went wrong?

articles.title: Chrome Can Now Pull Details From Your Gmail to Fill Out Web Forms - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Google began rolling out Chrome's enhanced autofill on Oct. 28, letting Gemini search a user's Gmail for order numbers, tracking information and flight bookings to fill web forms.
- The feature is available to U.S. users of Gemini in Chrome who have Personal Intelligence turned on, on desktop, Android and iOS.
- Google says sensitive data is encrypted and users can manage the feature in Chrome settings; its announcement does not list credit cards or addresses as data pulled from Gmail.
Google’s Chrome browser can now pull personal details from your Gmail inbox to fill out online forms for you, the company said in its announcement on Wednesday.
The update, called “enhanced autofill,” suggests order numbers, tracking information, and flight bookings when a form asks for them, wrote Amanda Lim, a Chrome product manager, in the announcement. Autofill is the browser tool that types in details like your name and address so you don’t have to.
It runs on Gemini, Google’s AI assistant, through a feature called Personal Intelligence, which lets Gemini draw on connected apps such as Gmail and Google Photos to tailor its answers to your own life. It is rolling out to Gemini in Chrome users who have Personal Intelligence turned on, on desktop, Android and iOS, starting in the U.S.
Google’s post names only those three kinds of data as coming from Gmail. Credit card numbers and addresses are part of Chrome’s standard autofill, which fills them from details you have saved in the browser, and the announcement does not say the new feature pulls them out of your inbox.
“You can manage whether enhanced autofill is enabled and what it can access via your Chrome settings,” Lim wrote. “As always, sensitive data is encrypted and you remain in control.”
Encryption scrambles data so only Google and other authorized parties can read it, though the post does not explain how that applies to the Gmail content Chrome reads or what it scans.
“Built with privacy in mind, Gemini and AI Mode don’t train directly on your Gmail inbox or Google Photos library,” Google said in March, when it began expanding Personal Intelligence to free U.S. users. AI Mode is Google’s AI-powered experience inside Search.
Users choose whether to connect their apps and can switch the connections off at any time, the post says, though Google does train on limited information, such as specific prompts and the model’s responses.
In November, users pushed back on a Smart Features setting that let Gemini analyze emails and calendars unless they opted out, and Google said it had not changed its underlying data-handling practices.
Google also revised its privacy policy effective Oct. 16, adding an exception to its pledge not to use Gmail, Drive, and Photos content for ads: personalized ads can draw on that data if users choose to make it available to other Google services that support them. Google says the content is not used for ad targeting by default and that advertisers do not get access to the contents of Gmail, Drive, or Photos.
Chrome has about 65% of the browser market, and in January Google gave paying U.S. subscribers an AI browsing agent called auto browse, which clicks through websites and fills out forms on a user’s behalf.
Chrome also dropped a line from its settings saying on-device AI, meaning models that run on your own computer rather than Google’s servers, works without sending data to Google servers. Google said the wording change did not reflect a change in how it handles on-device AI.
The rollout began Wednesday in the U.S. on desktop, Android and iOS, and Google’s announcement gives no date for other countries

articles.title: Kalshi Valuation Jumps to $40B after Latest Funding Round
articles.text:
Kalshi raises $1B at $40B valuation as non-sports revenue run rate tops $1B
The funding round comes as Kalshi expands its partnerships with the NBA and S&P Dow Jones Indices while facing legal challenges over its sports contracts.
Prediction market platform Kalshi has closed a $1 billion funding round at a $40 billion valuation, Reuters reported Thursday, as the company expands beyond sports betting into financial markets.
The Series G round was co-led by Wellington Management and Sequoia Capital. Kalshi also said its non-sports markets now generate more than $1 billion in annualized revenue, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The financing was first reported in September, when Kalshi was said to be seeking $1 billion at the same valuation. Thursday’s announcement confirmed the completion of the round.
Kalshi was valued at $22 billion in May, when it completed a $1 billion Series F funding round led by Coatue Management. At the time, the company reported an annualized revenue run rate exceeding $1.5 billion.
Kalshi recorded approximately $15.8 billion in trading volume over the past 30 days, according to DefiLlama data.
Expanding partnerships amid legal challenges
Kalshi has continued to expand its partnerships despite mounting legal challenges across the US. On Monday, the NBA named Kalshi and Polymarket preferred prediction market exchanges, while S&P Dow Jones Indices partnered with Kalshi to bring its financial benchmarks to event contracts.
The agreements come amid a legal dispute over whether Kalshi’s sports contracts are subject to state gambling laws or federal derivatives regulation. Utah sued the company last week, prompting a separate lawsuit from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Tuesday seeking to block state enforcement. On Wednesday, Utah escalated the dispute by filing criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders, according to a Reuters’ report.
Magazine: Private, fast USDT is coming to Bitcoin. Can it compete with Ethereum and Tron?

articles.title: Polymarket Pauses Trading as Prediction Market Investigates Security Incident - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Polymarket put its exchange in cancel-only mode and paused relayer actions as users report funds withdrawn without permission.
- A wallet flagged as the suspected attacker’s holds about $2.65 million in POL, per Arkham data, after multiple USDC.e-to-POL swaps through Relay.
- Hudson Rock says a DebugBear-hosted script containing wallet-draining code hard-codes that same address as its fallback recipient.
Polymarket users are reporting that the prediction market’s frontend may be compromised, with assets being withdrawn from accounts without permission.
The platform’s status page shows its trading API in a major outage and the exchange in cancel-only mode, meaning traders can pull existing orders but not place new ones. Relayer actions, which submit users’ signed transactions to the blockchain, are also paused.
Polymarket later confirmed that one its third-party providers was compromised. "We have referred this to relevant law enforcement," the company said on X. "Anyone who has been impacted will be made whole."
We've identified & fixed an issue impacting our international platform, Polymarket.com. One of our 3rd party providers was compromised, and we have referred this to relevant law enforcement.
Anyone who has been impacted will be made whole.
Out of an abundance of caution, we…
— Polymarket Traders (@PolymarketTrade) October 29, 2026
Arkham data shows that a wallet identified as the suspected attacker’s, 0x3F99139F1C5854bb628c2e576Aaf638e99dFfc18, holds about $2.65 million in POL, Polygon’s native token. It received multiple recent swaps from USDC.e, a bridged version of the USDC stablecoin, into POL through Relay, a cross-chain swapping service.
The first transactions began about an hour ago, and the wallet has shown no activity in the last five minutes.
Researchers at Hudson Rock said a script loaded from DebugBear, a web performance monitoring service, contains code that looks for a logged-in user’s trading session and attempts to sell their positions and transfer the assets.
The firm said the same wallet address is hard-coded in the script as its fallback recipient, and that Polymarket’s production site code records the script’s removal. Hudson Rock said it has not established how the compromise started or how many users were affected.
Polymarket has not yet said what caused the incident. In May, a private key compromise drained roughly $700,000 from an internal top-up wallet. A month later, a compromised third-party vendor let hackers inject malicious code into the frontend and steal about $3 million from fewer than 15 accounts, and Polymarket promised to refund users in full.
Editor's note: This story was updated after publication for clarity and to include additional details from Polymarket.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Spikes to $81,500 After Strong US Macro Data
articles.text:
Bitcoin price jumps to $81.5K as US GDP data beats expectations
BTC price action returned to a key weekly resistance level as US stock markets digested Alphabet’s Q3 earnings miss.
Bitcoin (BTC) rebounded above $81,000 after Thursday’s Wall Street open as US GDP numbers stayed strong and inflation data conformed to estimates.
Key points:
- Bitcoin jumped to $81,547 on the back of strong US macro data, dismissing Alphabet’s Q3 earnings miss.
- US PCE data conformed to expectations at 3.6% year-on-year, while Q3 GDP came in higher at 3.4% versus 3.2% expected.
- BTC/USD needs to reclaim $81,400 by the weekly close, per analysis by Rekt Capital.
Bitcoin brushes off Alphabet earnings miss
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD reaching $81,547 on Bitstamp after dropping as low as $79,607 following Wednesday’s daily close.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The September print of the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, acknowledged as Fed policymakers’ favorite indicator, showed an increase of 0.5% versus August and 3.6% year-on-year.
“Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 3.1 percent from one year ago,” an official release from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) stated.
US PCE index one-month % change. Source: BEA
The final estimate for Q3 GDP was 3.4%, above expectations of 3.2%. Speaking to CNBC, Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds, described economic growth “powering ahead despite the uncertainty of geopolitical risks and the damage posed to many sectors of the economy by higher energy costs.”
“The economy was thought to have been a lost cause during much of the current Administration’s time in office, but real GDP has bounced back above a 3% run rate in Q3 2026 for the first time in a year,” he noted.
US stock markets nonetheless opened lower, led by tech giant Alphabet, which fell 12% on the back of missed earnings and Q3 revenue figures.
Alphabet stock one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
At the latest meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Wedneaday, the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at 3.75-4%, also in line with what markets had anticipated. In a subsequent statement, chair Kevin Warsh said that the economic activity was “expanding at a strong pace,” while describing inflation as “elevated.”
“While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little,” he added.
Analyst sees $81,400 reclaim as key for weekly close
BTC price action still contended with overhead resistance on low time frames, with crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital seeing $81,400 as the nearest hurdle for buyers to overcome.

“Bitcoin is experiencing lots of zig-zagging relative to both the Weekly levels of ~$80400 and $81400 And this will probably continue going into the new Weekly Close,” he wrote in his latest analysis on X.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
Rekt Capital thus saw the need to reclaim $81,400 by the weekly candle close. The monthly close, meanwhile, was set to see BTC/USD drop 3.3% in October. Previously, Cointelegraph reported that the month of October has produced average returns of 26% since 2010.

articles.title: Hackers Publish Work Details of 41,000 Homeland Security Employees - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Distributed Denial of Secrets published a dataset called Icepick on Oct. 28 with work details for 41,191 DHS employees and contractors, including 21,329 from Customs and Border Protection and about 10,000 from ICE.
- A hacktivist group called the Department of Peace says it took the records from an Okta login service used by DHS, while Okta says it has no evidence its systems were compromised.
- DHS says it is aware of a potential breach and has filed a takedown notice; a sample of named employees has been matched to other records but the full archive has not been verified.
Names, job titles, office locations, and phone numbers for more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors were published online Wednesday by a transparency nonprofit.
The nonprofit says a hacktivist group, meaning hackers driven by politics rather than profit, gave it the records.
The department oversees border protection, immigration enforcement, and cybersecurity, so the file works like a directory of who does what, who reports to whom and how to reach them.
Transparency groups say the contact details are useful for public-records requests. Security researchers warn the same list could help anyone who wants to impersonate a supervisor over the phone or work out who sits behind a sensitive investigation.
The nonprofit, Distributed Denial of Secrets, publishes leaked documents and calls this dataset Icepick. It says the hackers, who call themselves the Department of Peace, took the records from an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS, a login system that lets employees open many internal tools with one account.
Okta, the company behind that login service, disputes the claim. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” the company told Reuters.
The group says it acted after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin pledged stepped-up operations by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, known as ICE. “On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was ‘turning up the heat.’ This is what happens to ICE when you do that,” a spokesperson for the group said. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” the hackers wrote.
The searchable archive indexes 41,191 people, including 21,329 from Customs and Border Protection and about 10,000 from ICE, a third of them in its investigative arm, Homeland Security Investigations.
It also lists more than 55,000 internal permission groups, which are labels that control who can open which systems, along with each person’s name, title, office, email, phone number and manager. DDoSecrets co-founder Emma Best says the dataset contains no home addresses.
“DHS is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively,” a department spokesperson said.
DHS has also filed a takedown notice through the security firm ZeroFox, asking the domain registrar to stop serving contact and location data of people who did not consent to its publication. The search site built on the data stopped loading Thursday, with its domain showing a registrar hold, and Bluesky is blocking links to the nonprofit hosting the archive.
In September, the cybercrime group ShinyHunters claimed to hold 2 to 3 terabytes of data on FBI agents and job applicants, and the bureau told staff to assume hackers have their personal data.
The newest records in the archive date to August 19, and some entries, including CISA staff who have since left the agency, are already out of date.

articles.title: French Senate Adopts Bill for Automatic Sharing of Crypto Tax Data
articles.text:
French Senate adopts bill for automatic sharing of crypto tax data
The French Senate adopted a bill authorizing the automatic exchange of crypto-asset tax information between international tax authorities, pending completion of the legislative process.
The French Senate adopted a bill to allow tax authorities to automatically exchange crypto transaction data with their foreign counterparts.
The bill passed its first reading on Tuesday and was then transmitted to the National Assembly as Bill no. 3421 for consideration.
The bill covers an agreement on exchanging crypto tax information and an update to an existing agreement on financial account information.
The crypto agreement is based on the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), developed by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). CARF sets common standards for participating jurisdictions to collect and automatically exchange information on crypto transactions.
France already introduced crypto reporting obligations through the 2025 Finance Act, implementing the crypto reporting amendment to the European Union’s Directive on Administrative Cooperation, known as DAC8. The rules require crypto service providers to report customer identities and transaction data to tax authorities, which share the information with authorities in users’ EU countries of residence.
French lawmakers are also debating crypto tax changes in the 2027 budget. The National Assembly adopted an amendment on Oct. 16 that would make gains from conversions into certain fiat-pegged stablecoins taxable from Jan. 1, 2027. The measure is not law yet.
Lawmakers resumed debate on the budget’s revenue section on Tuesday, with a vote scheduled for Nov. 3.
Related: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027
EU’s planned crypto tax repository raises data security, wrench attack concerns
Tax reporting under DAC8 raises data security concerns because it involves sharing personal information, including names, addresses, tax numbers and transaction volumes, between EU tax authorities, Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph.
“In a country where crypto holders have been physically targeted, a leaked list of who trades what, and for how much, is not only a privacy issue but first and foremost a safety issue.” 
The European Commission plans to create a central repository for crypto reports by the end of 2026. Each member state’s tax authorities would be able to access information concerning its tax residents.
Fleuret said that centralizing this information could create a “single point of failure” for sensitive crypto transaction data.
Share of wrench attacks by region. Source: CertiK
Fleuret’s remarks follow an alarming rise in physical attacks targeting cryptocurrency investors, also known as wrench attacks. During the first half of 2026, France accounted for 33 of the 52 verified wrench attacks worldwide, according to blockchain security company CertiK.
In a March incident, a French couple in their late 50s was robbed of about $1 million worth of Bitcoin by criminals posing as police officers.
Magazine: France is world’s most dangerous place for Bitcoiners: 90 attacks in 7 months

articles.title: Crypto Spends $176 Million on Midterms, But Only 13% of Voters See It as a Priority - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Only 13% of Americans say it’s very important that candidates support emerging technologies like crypto and DeFi, the survey found.
- A broader pitch, keeping fintech builders in the U.S., ranks highest at 35%, with Republicans ahead of Democrats 45% to 30%.
- The crypto industry has spent about $176 million on more than 100 midterm races this cycle, according to a Reuters review.
The crypto industry is spending heavily on next week’s midterm elections. Voters aren’t putting it near the top of their lists.
Only 13% of Americans say it’s extremely or very important that a political candidate supports the growth of emerging financial technologies like blockchain, crypto and decentralized finance, according to a survey conducted by Ipsos for the DeFi Education Fund, a crypto policy advocacy group.
A broader pitch fared better. About 35% say it’s very important that candidates ensure those building the next generation of financial technology are encouraged to do so in the U.S., the top-ranked policy position in the survey. Just 26% said the same about supporting new rules that allow innovation in the financial system.
The DeFi Education Fund describes the results as “bipartisan support for U.S. innovation,” and the narrower crypto question shows little partisan gap: 15% of Republicans and 13% of Democrats rate it very important. But on the top-ranked item, Republicans led Democrats 45% to 30%.
The survey polled 1,545 adults from Sept. 8 to 16 on Ipsos’ KnowledgePanel, the probability-based panel the Federal Reserve uses for its household finance survey, with a margin of error of plus or minus 2.8 percentage points. Party identification includes independents who lean toward a party.
The industry’s spending tells a different story. Crypto groups have spent about $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this cycle, according to a Reuters review, with super PAC Fairshake and its affiliates accounting for about $150.8 million through Oct. 20.
One Fairshake affiliate has disclosed more than $46 million in spending against former Sen. Sherrod Brown in Ohio’s Senate race.
The stakes are high for the industry after the Clarity Act, which would have set federal rules for crypto markets, failed a key Senate vote in September amid disputes over ethics provisions covering President Donald Trump’s crypto interests. Since then, the industry has turned to regulators like the SEC and CFTC to write the rules instead.
The survey suggests voters care more about security and control than about crypto itself. Some 63% say the financial system needs an upgrade to combat threats like AI and cybercrime, and 49% say the government shouldn’t decide which products they can invest in.

articles.title: Bank of England Opens Consultation on Tokenized Collateral for Clearing
articles.text:
Bank of England opens consultation on tokenized collateral for clearing
Central counterparties would need to show tokenized collateral meets liquidity and risk tests under proposed Bank of England guidance.
The Bank of England has opened a consultation on how a central counterparty (CCP) can accept digital versions of eligible collateral, saying existing rules allow it when assets meet clearing standards.
The draft supervisory statement would clarify what CCPs must address in applications under the current approval process. It covers collateral already accepted and types that qualify under the proposed UK CCP Rulebook but are not in use. The statement would not create new regulatory obligations.
The BoE said tokenized collateral must remain capable of being valued, transferred and realized, including in stressed conditions. Faster movement across jurisdictions could help firms meet margin calls, it said.
“Through today’s consultation, the Bank is further delivering its secondary objective for innovation in financial market infrastructure, while maintaining financial stability. It’s part of a major agenda between authorities and industry to enable the responsible adoption of tokenisation in financial markets,” Sarah Breeden, deputy governor for financial stability, said.
The consultation paper closes Feb. 12, 2027. The central bank expects to publish its policy response and rules later this quarter.

articles.title: $11 Billion in Bitcoin Options Expire Tomorrow—Here's What It Means - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- About $11 billion in Bitcoin options, roughly 135,000 BTC and a third of Deribit's Bitcoin options open interest, expire on Friday.
- Max pain, the price where option sellers pay out the least, sits at $78,000 against a market price near $81,500, and about 86% of the contracts are out of the money.
- The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote with two dissenters favoring a hike, and the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.05%.
About $11 billion in Bitcoin options expire on Friday on Deribit, a crypto options exchange, with Bitcoin trading near $81,500 a day after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady while two of its officials voted to raise them.
Even people who never touch options have a stake, because the traders who sold these contracts must buy or sell real Bitcoin to hedge as the price moves, which can add to swings without any news behind them.
An option is a contract that gives its holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (a call) or sell (a put) Bitcoin at a fixed price, called the strike, by a set date. Friday’s batch covers about 135,000 Bitcoin in contracts, roughly 88,700 calls and 46,500 puts, per Deribit’s data.
That equals about a third of all Bitcoin options open on the exchange and roughly 70% more than the $6.4 billion that expired in August. The put-to-call ratio, which compares bets on a drop with bets on a rally, is 0.52, so calls outnumber puts nearly two to one, which means there’s optimism in terms of price going up.
The $11 billion is notional value, the face value of the contracts at today’s price, not money changing hands. About 86% of the contracts are out of the money, meaning they would be worthless at current prices, and settling at today’s level would move roughly $130 million, about 1% of the headline figure.
Traders watch the Bitcoin options expiry day as one of the key events for their fundamental analysis. Another catalyst to consider is the Federal Reserve’s policy on rates. The Fed yesterday held firm at 3.75% to 4.00%, with expectations rising for another hike this year. Interest rates impact the whole economy as investment in risky assets and businesses would be less attractive than lending giving your money to the government through Treasuries.
Traders also watch max pain, the price at which the most contracts expire worthless and sellers pay out the least. Deribit’s open interest puts it at $78,000, about $3,500 below the market, though it describes positioning and does not predict where Bitcoin will settle. After all, this is crypto, and wild movements are not a strange occurrence.
The heaviest call bets sit at $95,000 and $100,000, about 16% and 23% above the current price, while the biggest put cluster is at $70,000, about 14% below. Friday’s expiry also saw the most trading of any Bitcoin options expiry on Deribit over the past 24 hours, with more than 6,000 contracts changing hands
Friday’s batch is smaller than the $15 billion expiry in March, but about three times the $3.6 billion expiry from April 2021.
The next test is December 25, when about 135,500 Bitcoin in options are already set to expire, roughly the same size as Friday’s and about two weeks after the Fed meets December 8-9.

articles.title: Canton Foundation Backs RedStone Pricing Tool With $1.52M
articles.text:
Canton Foundation grants RedStone 15.8M Canton Coin for pricing standard
RedStone’s planned pricing tool will let institutions on Canton use shared market prices without exposing deal terms to data providers.
The Canton Foundation approved almost 15.8 million Canton Coin (worth about $1.55 million at the time of writing) to fund RedStone’s open-source pricing tool for institutions.
The CC token, last trading at roughly $0.0979, has a market cap of $3.91 billion, according to Coingecko data, with $23.23 million in trading the past 24 hours.
The Canton Access and Privacy Standard (CAPS) is designed to let institutions use a shared market price to value transactions without revealing their agreed settlement amounts to data providers, according to Thursday’s announcement shared with Cointelegraph.
“By supporting open-source initiatives like CAPS, the Foundation is helping establish a shared privacy and licensing framework that enables multiple data providers to serve the network,” said Viv Diwakar, head of the Canton Foundation.
Under the standard, the blockchain oracle provider, will publish a reference price that can be used to calculate transaction values.
Initial development will cover pricing for tokenized funds, private-market assets and structured products. The pricing calculations and licensing module will be released under the Apache 2.0 open-source license, which allows other providers to adapt them.
RedStone has provided pricing data on Canton since December 2025 and works with ecosystem participants including Temple Digital Group, according to the company.
Canton Network said in a May blog post that it had onboarded more than 600 institutions, including Goldman Sachs, DTCC, BNY and Franklin Templeton, and was processing around $9 trillion in monthly transaction volume.
