articles.title: 4M Bitcoin Bought Above $85K Could Cap Recovery: Glassnode - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Long-term Bitcoin holders own about 4 million BTC bought between $85,000 and $118,000, mostly in 2025, according to on-chain analytics firm Glassnode.
- Bloomberg Intelligence puts the average cost basis of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holders just under $82,000, with Bitcoin trading around $81,600.
- The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with traders putting the odds of a December hike above 70% beforehand.
Bitcoin's long-term holders are sitting on losses on about 4 million BTC bought between $85,000 and $118,000, and many may sell if the price climbs back toward that level, according to a note from on-chain analytics firm Glassnode.
Glassnode, which defines long-term holders as those holding coins for more than 155 days, said most of that block was bought in 2025. More than half of all long-term holder coins were bought above the current price, according to the note, published Wednesday ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision.
$85K keeps turning $BTC back. Since January, Bitcoin has closed above it on only five days, never more than three in a row. It's a truly tough level to break. More in depth analysis in our latest Week on Chain report https://t.co/xy8lE3ilt3
— glassnode (@glassnode) October 28, 2026
That block is worth about $326 billion at Bitcoin's current price of around $81,400, up 1.2% over the past 24 hours but about 35% below its all-time high of $126,080.
Glassnode said a band between $84,000 and $85,000 has turned Bitcoin back four times this year, and that the asset has closed above it on only five days since January. Bitcoin last broke above it in September, peaking at $87,100.
ETF holders are near break-even too. Glassnode puts the average price U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs paid for their coins at $81,500. Bloomberg Intelligence ETF analyst James Seyffart estimated the figure at just under $82,000 in a tweet on Wednesday, adding that Bitcoin has hovered around that level since the end of August.
Seyffart's chart put ETF holders' average unrealized loss at about $2.63 billion as of Monday. In replies, he said the estimate tracks only fund flows, not what secondary-market buyers paid.
Rates, flows and the carry trade
The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Traders had put the odds of another quarter-point hike in December above 70% before the decision.
Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, argued that a December hike had been priced in to a certain extent. "What truly constrains Bitcoin's performance," he told Decrypt, "is the persistently high U.S. Treasury yields and real interest rates, which are significantly raising the opportunity cost for investors holding risk assets."
The 10-year Treasury yield stood just under 5% at midday on Thursday, according to CNBC, down from 5.05% at Wednesday's close and a 52-week high of 5.37% on October 7.
Sun added that lower funding rates on Bitcoin perpetual futures have squeezed returns on cash-and-carry arbitrage, which pairs spot Bitcoin with short futures. Galaxy Research found that nine hedge funds and banks cut 68,000 BTC worth of spot ETF exposure as that trade dried up, while wealth platforms and sovereign funds added.
ETF flows have picked up this week. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $424 million from Monday to Wednesday, per SoSoValue data, after $635 million left the funds on October 22.
"Any rally above $85,000 could face selling pressure from long-term holders seeking to break even," Sun said, echoing Glassnode.
Both pointed to light selling, however. Glassnode said holders have realized smaller losses with each dip since August: at the August low, realized losses outweighed profits by about $630 million in a day, while around a dip on October 24 the largest daily net loss was about $27 million.
"The core issue facing the market right now is not panic selling, but rather insufficient new buying interest to support a sustained recovery," Sun said.
On the downside, Glassnode pointed to about $42 million in bids between $78,000 and $79,000 on Binance, and the average cost basis of newer buyers at $75,800.
Sun expects Bitcoin to keep trading between $75,000 and $85,000 in the short term until macro liquidity improves and ETFs resume continuous net inflows. Whether selling pressure near $85,000 can be absorbed "will serve as an important signal to determine whether the market can regain strength," he said.

articles.title: Brazil Crypto Rules Leave Questions as Deadline Nears
articles.text:
Brazil’s Halloween eve crypto deadline brings more tricks than treats
Brazil’s crypto exchanges face an application deadline on Friday, with costly requirements and unanswered regulatory questions complicating compliance.
Cryptocurrency exchanges operating in Brazil face mounting compliance costs and unanswered regulatory questions ahead of a license application deadline.
Exchanges already operating in Brazil must apply for authorization by Friday to continue operating, but the cutoff date is just the start of a lengthy compliance process.
“Filing is the easy part,” Fabio Cendão, founding partner at Brazilian law firm FCM Law, told Cointelegraph, pointing to challenges such as high capital requirements, complex compliance obligations and recurring audits.
Brazil introduced its crypto regulatory framework in November 2025, setting rules for exchanges, custodians and other virtual asset service providers under the supervision of its central bank, the Banco Central do Brasil (BCB).
Brazil ranks as the world’s top country for grassroots crypto adoption, recording $252.5 billion in crypto activity between July 2025 and June 2026, according to Chainalysis.
What happens after the deadline?
Crypto platforms that apply on time can continue operating while regulators review their applications, which can take up to two years, according to Cendão.
New entrants must obtain authorization before launching regulated services.
Related: Brazil’s Petrobras uses Cardano to track sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel
Companies that miss the deadline must stop providing services within 30 days from Friday, said Marcelo de Castro Cunha Filho, a lawyer at Machado Meyer. From Nov. 6, banks and payment institutions will also face restrictions on conducting crypto transactions with unauthorized providers.
Regulatory questions remain unresolved
Under Brazil’s new rules, crypto service providers must verify the origin and destination of crypto transfers, including those involving self-custodial wallets. The rules also impose a $100,000 limit on certain international crypto transfers when the counterparty is not authorized to operate in Brazil’s foreign exchange market.
Binance Brazil general manager Thiago Sarandy told Cointelegraph that questions remain over how exchanges should identify self-custody wallets, interpret a $100,000 operational limit and determine minimum transaction-reporting thresholds.
“The lack of clarity creates a risky situation,” Sarandy said, warning that exchanges may report fragmented or inconsistent data to the regulatory authorities, which “puts in jeopardy the oversight capacity.”
Related: France proposes liability for crypto exchanges offering DeFi access
Sarandy said industry association ABCripto had submitted questions to the BCB but had yet to receive answers.
Compliance costs threaten smaller exchanges
Major global exchanges have filed applications, including OKX, Binance and Coinbase. Meanwhile, Latin American crypto exchange Bitso is ending direct retail services in Brazil through a partnership with local exchange Mercado Bitcoin.
But smaller operators face a steeper challenge. FCM Law’s Cendão said minimum capital requirements range from 10.8 million Brazilian reais ($2 million) to 37.2 million reais, depending on the services offered, alongside technical certification, custody audits and anti-money laundering controls.
He warned that the costs could make compliance unviable for smaller exchanges, potentially increasing market concentration.
Cunha Filho of Machado Meyer also said it was unclear how exchanges that miss the deadline should return crypto to customers who have no accounts with authorized providers or have not agreed to transfer their assets.
The BCB did not respond to Cointelegraph’s request for comment by publication time.

HYPE, the token behind the Hyperliquid exchange, jumped about 13% on Thursday to roughly $91 after Intercontinental Exchange, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, announced a deal to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the United States.
The token climbed from a daily open of $80.69 to a high of $92.10 on KuCoin, leaving it about 7% below the record near $98 it set in September. Hyperliquid’s token now trades at around a $22.4 billion market capitalization.
ICE and Trade[XYZ], a company that runs markets for real-world assets on Hyperliquid, signed a definitive agreement that makes ICE the exclusive operator of Trade[XYZ]'s regulated markets, and ICE is taking a strategic stake in the company.
ICE will build a dedicated retail market and clearing structure for the product, which still needs regulatory approvals and has no launch date.
We're honored to have your trust and support. https://t.co/1bCLPHbAcy
— trade.xyz (@tradexyz) October 29, 2026
Perpetual futures are derivatives with no expiry date that let traders take leveraged positions, meaning bets amplified with borrowed money. Trade[XYZ] already offers eligible users outside the U.S. around-the-clock perpetuals on stocks, equity indices, commodities and currencies, while Hyperliquid provides the underlying infrastructure.
Stan Druckenmiller, the macro investor who ran the Duquesne Capital hedge fund for about 30 years and said it never had a losing year, publicly backed the deal as an investor in Trade[XYZ]. “I am excited to be an investor in trade(xyz) as they partner with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States,” Druckenmiller wrote on X. “As a market participant, I am looking forward to using their innovative product to enhance my investment process.
The U.S. markets are meant to comply with know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering rules, which require identity checks, and ICE will seek approvals to support leveraged trading.
Verified customers would connect through futures commission merchants, the brokers that handle customer futures accounts, and ICE plans to distribute the product through its joint venture with OKX, which has its own approvals pending. ICE bought into OKX at a $25 billion valuation in March.
ICE Chair and CEO Jeffrey Sprecher described the perpetuals as “additive to our futures markets, not a replacement for them.” ICE says more than 99% of its participation today is institutional, so retail traders are a new business, and it will run the unit separately from its institutional futures and clearing franchise.
President Donald Trump said in August that the CFTC was working to let Hyperliquid operate legally in the United States, where the exchange is currently geofenced.

articles.title: USDT on Bitcoin: Can Utexo Compete With Ethereum and Tron?
articles.text:
Private, fast USDT is coming to Bitcoin. Can it compete with Ethereum and Tron?
USDT is coming home to Bitcoin, offering privacy and Lightning-fast payments. But can Bitcoin’s revamped version of Tether compete with stablecoins on ETH and TRON?
Utexo is preparing to bring Tether’s dollar-backed stablecoin back to Bitcoin after a three-year hiatus.
The Dubai-based blockchain startup says it will achieve the integration through RGB, a protocol that keeps asset transaction data off-chain.
The public launch is scheduled for Nov. 28, with Lightning Network support planned for Q1 2027, promising private transfers and fast payments via Bitcoin’s payment network.
But with $300 billion of stablecoin supply already circulating on networks like Ethereum and Tron, why would users want to transact on a slower network that doesn’t offer smart contracts or DeFi? Can it compete with the stablecoin incumbents?
$300 billion of stablecoin supply. Source: DeFiLlama
Why bring USDT back to Bitcoin?
This isn’t the first time we’ve seen USDT on Bitcoin. It actually began life as a stablecoin on Bitcoin in 2014 through the Omni protocol, but Tether eventually halted issuance in August 2023, citing declining usage.
Tether then announced plans to launch USDT on RGB in August 2025. That didn’t happen, however, Tether subsequently led Utexo’s $7.5 million seed round in March, and the new firm will launch the Bitcoin version of the stablecoin using Tether’s USDT0 protocol.
But if usage of USDT on Bitcoin had declined to the point it was no longer viable the first time around, why would it be more popular now? What has changed since 2023?
Viktor Ihnatiuk, co-founder and chief executive of Utexo, tells Magazine the answer is two-fold: Speed and privacy. Using Bitcoin for the settlement layer, and RGB to keep transaction details off the public blockchain, makes private and fast transactions a reality.
“You can actually achieve any speed you want to achieve,” he says. “Bitcoin is the best blockchain. Lightning is the best technology to scale payments.”
RGB Protocol Documentation. Source: RGB
Utexo grew out of an effort to bring dollar-denominated payments to Bitcoin, and Ihnatiuk says the idea took shape after a conversation with Tether at Bitcoin Prague in 2023.
The company also builds on RGB and Lightning infrastructure developed by ThunderStack, founded by fellow Utexo co-founder Renat Skitsan.
What is RGB, and how does it work?
RGB has been in development since 2016 and was designed to let users issue and transfer digital assets through contracts tied to Bitcoin, without recording every transaction detail on its public blockchain.
Rather than making Bitcoin behave like Ethereum, on RGB, the parties validate asset transactions themselves, while cryptographic commitments anchored to Bitcoin help secure the system. That means RGB is a Bitcoin-native protocol rather than a sidechain or rollup.
RGB also works with the Lightning Network, enabling USDT to move through its payment channels without each transfer requiring a base-layer transaction.
“Lightning allows you to do transactions with a dynamic of 100 milliseconds,” Ihnatiuk says. “It’s faster than Solana, it’s faster than Monad, it’s faster than Sui or Aptos. The limitation is only in the brain of people who don’t understand how to scale Bitcoin.”
Bitcoin’s transparency has hampered business adoption, as many firms like to keep their purchases and transaction counterparts confidential.
Ihnatiuk says that rather than compete with networks like Tron on retail transaction volume or Ethereum on decentralized finance, the company believes the combination of secure Bitcoin-based settlement and greater transaction confidentiality will be enough to persuade businesses to make the switch.
Utexo can also selectively disclose relevant transaction information for compliance purposes, Ihnatiuk says, and has procedures for responding to law enforcement requests.
Related: Is Bitcoin kidding itself about the Lightning Network?
2026 institutional investor survey. Source: Coinbase and EY-Parthenon
Bridge over troubled waters
Utexo opened early access to its USDT Mint product on Oct. 22, allowing verified professional operators, like exchanges, wallets and market makers, to test minting, confidential transfers and redemption on Bitcoin’s Signet test network.
The sandbox gives operators time to test transaction flows and prepare integrations ahead of the public launch at the end of November, after which time Ihnatiuk predicts “everything will become so big.”
But getting existing USDT onto Bitcoin through Utexo Mint involves an additional step. The service locks USDT0 on Arbitrum before minting an equivalent amount of USDT on Bitcoin. Users can redeem their tokens by burning the RGB asset and triggering the release of the corresponding funds on the source network.
Related: Tether says it helped freeze $550M in Iran-linked USDT this year
That means Mint’s security also depends on the mechanisms connecting the networks, not on Bitcoin and RGB alone.
Users need to trust that the USDT0 locked on Arbitrum remains available and can be released when they redeem their Bitcoin-based USDT. Bridges have historically acted like honeypots to hackers, so this architecture introduces additional risk, even if the design attempts to mitigate them.
Utexo says Mint has been audited by Oxorio, although the full audit report is not publicly available.
What would success look like?
Utexo has named UniSat as a launch partner, with plans to support USDT transfers and swaps through its wallet, and Ihnatiuk says Utexo is working with 12 over-the-counter network partners and has another 40 in its pipeline.
Ihnatiuk sees opportunities in Bitcoin-native trading and lending, but he says Bitcoin won’t replicate Ethereum’s DeFi ecosystem; its strengths lie in payments and simpler financial arrangements like escrow-based exchanges.
“People who think that it’s possible to replicate Ethereum DeFi on Bitcoin make a huge mistake,” he says. “Bitcoin was never built for DeFi. Bitcoin was always built for payments.”
Another potential use case is helping keep miners on Bitcoin as they could swap BTC for USDT directly on Bitcoin rather than having to move funds to centralized exchanges. That would reduce their exposure to custodial risk and make it easier to automate hedging strategies. “So, for miners, it’s quite beneficial,” he says.
Ihnatiuk is setting an ambitious target for the first year.
“I would love to achieve our minimum milestone of $1 billion USDT on the Bitcoin network in the next 12 months,” he says. “My initial goal is $10 billion. My median goal is $5 billion.”
There is also a question about the benefits for Bitcoin itself. Ihnatiuk says greater USDT adoption will increase miner fee revenue.
“Once USDT comes back to Bitcoin,” he says, “you will get meaningful adoption; all the transactions will come to Bitcoin. So, yeah, miners will be able to make much more.”
So can Bitcoin compete with Ethereum, Tron and other networks as a new home for USDT? Possibly; it just needs to prove there’s a market this time around.
Related: ‘Bunker mode’ won’t protect your crypto, critics say

articles.title: Walmart Blocks Its Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Trading Venue - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna Group, Carnival and Arcos Dorados joined the list of companies objecting to OKXICE TSV, according to its Oct. 28 notice.
- The total has climbed from nine on Oct. 15 to 38, broadening the pushback into retail, health care and travel.
- Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, a timely objection bars the venue from listing a third-party tokenized version of a company’s stock.
The world’s largest retailer is now keeping its shares off OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.
Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna Group, Carnival, and Arcos Dorados have objected to having their shares offered on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated notice from the venue dated Wednesday. The five additions bring the total to 38 companies.
That’s up from 33 a day earlier, when JPMorgan Chase, Coca-Cola and Dell were among seven newcomers. The tally has more than quadrupled since the venue’s first list of nine objectors on Oct. 15. It grew to 16 on Oct. 19, with names including Microsoft, and 22 on Oct. 23 when Wells Fargo joined the list.
The latest batch broadens the pushback beyond tech and finance into retail, health care, and travel. Arcos Dorados, the largest McDonald’s franchisee in Latin America, joins McDonald’s itself, which objected earlier this month. Eli Lilly and Cigna join UnitedHealth Group and Moderna among the health care companies on the list.
The objections carry real weight. Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.
If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue, and the notices don’t disclose the companies’ reasons.
OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks around the clock. OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before announcing the 24/7 venue this month.
Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC. The exemption caps the venue at 75 of the largest, most liquid stocks, with trading limited to 0.25% of each stock’s average daily volume, and up to 250 other stocks at 2.5%.
The list may not be finished. Under the SEC’s order, companies have 30 days from receiving notice to object, and some of the market’s most heavily traded names, including Nvidia, Tesla, Apple and Amazon, haven’t done so.
The venue has also said it can list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, which would give companies direct control over how their stock appears onchain, though the notices don’t identify any such listings.

articles.title: Polygon Extends Its Stablecoin Payments Infrastructure to Solana - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Polygon Labs expanded its Open Money Stack—a bundle of stablecoin payments tools—to Solana.
- The platform aims to collapse the multi-provider complexity of crypto payments into one connection.
- The move rides Solana’s payments momentum and extends Polygon’s push, including its Coinme acquisition.
Polygon Labs is extending its stablecoin payments infrastructure to Solana, giving businesses on the rival network a single connection to pull money in from bank accounts, move crypto across chains, and pay out to customers and suppliers worldwide.
The company said the expansion brings its Open Money Stack, a bundle of payments tools, to Solana for the first time.
The pitch addresses a persistent headache in crypto payments: sending the tokens is the easy part, but getting money from a bank account into a wallet, converting it and landing it back in a recipient’s bank account typically requires stitching together several providers, each with its own integration and contract.
Open Money Stack collapses that into one technical connection and one commercial relationship, with businesses free to adopt the whole thing or mix individual pieces into their existing systems.
Through the platform, a Solana business can connect bank, card, cash, and crypto funding routes, spin up embedded wallets, route and convert funds across networks including Polygon, Ethereum and Tron, and deliver payouts into banks, cards, or wallets. A remittance provider, for instance, could take dollars from a sender, deliver USDC on Solana, and connect the recipient to a bank payout.
“Every bank and fintech that wants to use crypto faces the same problem: connecting them to the accounts and payment systems its customers already use,” said Sandeep Nailwal, co-founder and CEO of the Polygon Foundation, adding that adding Solana lets more businesses build on the network their customers choose.
Cross-border payments firm Kira is among the first to adopt Solana through the stack, using it to help clients turn stablecoin transfers into dollars in their bank accounts to pay overseas suppliers.
The move reflects Solana’s growing pull as a payments venue, having processed more than $5 trillion in stablecoin volume this year, per the Solana Foundation.
The network recently rolled out an institutional settlement standard with input from J.P. Morgan and went live with its Alpenglow upgrade. For Polygon, the expansion builds on its broader payments push, including its acquisition of crypto-cash firm Coinme.

articles.title: Polygon Expands Open Money Stack to Solana
articles.text:
Polygon expands Open Money Stack to Solana, after Tron rollout
The move follows the addition of Tron support and Polygon’s acquisition of Coinme.
Polygon Labs is expanding Open Money Stack, its suite of services connecting bank accounts, crypto wallets and payouts, to the Solana network.
The expansion lets businesses building on Solana use Open Money Stack to accept funding from bank accounts, provide customer wallets and arrange payouts.
Polygon Labs CEO Marc Boiron told Cointelegraph that customer demand and stablecoin activity drove the decision to expand to Solana and, earlier this month, Tron.
Solana recorded about $5.76 trillion in stablecoin transfers between Jan. 1 and Oct. 27, while Tron recorded $6.94 trillion in stablecoin transfers over the same period, according to Token Terminal data.
“As that activity grows, connecting Solana to bank accounts, wallets and global payout networks allows businesses to deliver stablecoin payments to more customers and markets,” said Vibhu Norby, chief product officer, Solana Foundation.
Polygon’s Trails service has supported transfers between Solana and Ethereum-compatible networks since August. The latest expansion adds access to bank, card and cash funding, customer accounts, embedded wallets and payouts through the same integration, Boiron said.
“We hear from businesses that their customers and payment activity are already spread across networks and that they don’t want to force a chain choice or stitch together a bank provider, wallet, routing service and payout partner for each one,” he said.
The broader stack was already available for eligible uses on Polygon, Ethereum and other Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) networks, he added.
Last year, ecosystem data provider The Grid cataloged 478 companies and 261 projects in the Solana ecosystem. Boiron said Kira, which provides US dollar accounts and stablecoin-based cross-border payment services to businesses, is among the first customers using the Solana integration.
The Solana expansion follows Polygon’s completed acquisition of Coinme, which gave its US payments business access to 37 money transmitter licenses and 11 state exemptions, covering 48 states.

articles.title: Justin Sun's HTX Agrees to Leave UK in Settlement With Financial Watchdog - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The FCA has settled its High Court case against HTX, securing undertakings that the exchange will not target or solicit UK consumers.
- HTX has stopped taking deposits and new sign-ups from the UK, and existing UK users have 48 hours to withdraw their assets, the exchange said.
- The case was the FCA's first against a crypto firm under UK financial promotion rules, and the terms of the settlement are confidential.
Crypto exchange HTX is leaving the UK after settling a lawsuit brought by the Financial Conduct Authority over illegal crypto promotions, the regulator said on Thursday.
The FCA said it had secured undertakings in the High Court that HTX, formerly known as Huobi, will not knowingly promote crypto services unlawfully to UK consumers. Huobi Global S.A., the Panama-registered company named as the first defendant, has undertaken not to communicate financial promotions in breach of UK law across HTX's website, apps and social media, according to the court order.
HTX, which names Tron founder Justin Sun as a global adviser, is no longer active in the UK, the regulator said. UK consumers can no longer make deposits, and new UK users cannot sign up.
"Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law," said Steve Smart, the FCA's executive director of enforcement and market oversight. "The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences."
HTX said it had "proactively implemented measures to align with the UK's financial promotion regulations," the Financial Times reported. On its website, the exchange said existing UK customers are blocked from trading and have 48 hours to withdraw their assets before their accounts are closed.
The terms of the settlement are confidential, and it does not amount to an admission of liability or wrongdoing, the FCA said.
The regulator began proceedings against HTX in October 2025, its first enforcement case against a crypto firm under the UK's financial promotion rules, saying the exchange had repeatedly failed to engage with it. The two sides began settlement talks in March, which were extended in June, according to court orders reported by Reuters.
In May, the UK sanctioned Huobi Global S.A. over alleged support for Russia's financial sector, with the government's notice listing HTX as another name for the designated entity.
Two months later, the European Union named Huobi Global in its 21st package of Russia sanctions, accusing it of "significantly frustrating" the bloc's measures and barring EU transactions with the exchange, though stopping short of a full asset freeze. HTX has said Huobi Global S.A. is "distinct from the online HTX exchange."

articles.title: Chainalysis Maps DPRK Crypto Cash-Outs After OFAC Sanctions
articles.text:
Chainalysis traces North Korean crypto cash-outs through Garantex
The analysis followed US sanctions against 10 people and one entity accused of helping North Korean IT worker schemes fund weapons programs.
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis mapped a long-running network of Russian intermediaries that helped North Korean IT workers cash out millions of dollars in cryptocurrency.
The US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity on Wednesday for supporting North Korean government-run IT worker schemes that it said funded the country’s weapons programs, according to a press release.
Those sanctioned included Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas. Treasury said Boykov had converted about $3.5 million in crypto for sanctioned company Alis since 2024, while Obertas had handled nearly $2 million in crypto conversions for North Korean officials since January 2025.
In one example, a wallet linked to a North Korean IT worker received regular stablecoin payments, converted them into Ether (ETH) and transferred the funds through consolidation addresses to Boykov, according to Chainalysis’ Wednesday report. Boykov then sent the cryptocurrency to Russian exchange Garantex to cash out.
North Korean IT workers using false identities to obtain jobs at crypto companies have posed a persistent security threat. In June 2025, the US Department of Justice announced charges against four North Korean nationals over a scheme involving fraudulent IT employment and the theft of more than $900,000 from US and Serbian crypto companies.

articles.title: Morning Minute: Hedge Funds Left the BTC ETF Trade and Sovereign Wealth Stepped In - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors rebound fall 1-2% alongside stocks; BTC at $80k
- HYPE soars on news of partnership with NYSE to bring perps to the US
- BTC ETFs see another $137M net inflows, flipping October green
- Visa stablecoin settlement volume 10x’s year over year
- YCombinator names its 6 crypto focus areas focused around crypto AI, stablecoins, and tokenization
Hedge Funds Left the BTC ETF Trade and Sovereign Wealth Stepped In
Every quarter, big institutions have to tell the SEC what they own. Add up those filings from just before Bitcoin’s October 2025 high through the end of June, and the picture is clear: nine hedge funds and banks sold about 68,000 Bitcoin worth of ETF shares over those nine months, roughly $5.4 billion at today’s prices. Millennium, Brevan Howard, Goldman Sachs, D.E. Shaw and five others led the selling. Some trimmed by a third. Some sold everything.
The trade had nothing to do with believing in Bitcoin. You buy the ETF, you simultaneously bet against Bitcoin in the futures market, and you pocket the gap between those two prices. Done right you make money whether Bitcoin rises or falls—as long as the gap beats what you’d earn just parking the cash in Treasury bills.
Before the high, that gap paid 7.9% a year, a full 3.9 points better than T-bills. By late October it paid 4.8%, barely half a point better. After fees and financing, Galaxy’s Alex Thorn figures what’s left is about 1.5 points over cash. Not worth the trouble.
“That arithmetic, not the price, is why the multi-strategy desks left,” he wrote.
You can see it in the futures data too. Both sides of that trade shrank by nearly identical amounts, around 57% each.
Now look at who came in and bought. Morgan Stanley’s wealth management arm. Mubadala. The Abu Dhabi Investment Council. Roughly 2,200 other filers added about 20,000 Bitcoin between them. Hedge funds sold; sovereign funds and wealth managers bought. And the investors too small to file at all—advisers, family offices, regular people—cut their holdings by just 6.6% while the price fell 49%. So Middle America is hodling.
That’s the whole story. The people who were never really Bitcoin investors left. The people who were didn’t flinch.
Since June, the funds have added back 87,000 Bitcoin—this time as straightforward buying, not arbitrage.
The rate picture is turning too. The Fed held Wednesday, but December has quietly softened: a month ago traders put 59% odds on two rate hikes by year-end. Today that’s zero. Expected tightening has been cut roughly in half. Less tightening helps every risk asset.
October’s flows already show the shift. The month was down $907 million at the midpoint. Through Tuesday it’s essentially flat, with $724 million arriving in just the last eight sessions.
The fast money is gone. The believers are left. And that’s the foundation you can build on for a bull market rally…

articles.title: Unlimit Founder Commits $45M to Phase AI Blockchain
articles.text:
Unlimit founder backs Phase blockchain with $45M as mainnet launches
Phase’s new network lets smartphone owners earn tokens for validating transactions and sharing internet connections with AI agents.
Phase, a new blockchain that lets smartphone users earn tokens by helping run AI services, has received a $45 million funding commitment from Unlimit founder Kirill Eves.
Phase announced the launch of its blockchain on Thursday alongside Phase Proxy, a service that routes AI agents’ web requests through internet connections shared via smartphones.
Phase has no outside investors, the company told Cointelegraph. Eves’ $45 million commitment covers its first two years of development and provides another two years of runway.
“Websites routinely block or rate-limit automated traffic originating from data centers, even when an agent is acting on a legitimate user request,” Eves told Cointelegraph. “As agents take on more tasks across multiple websites, these restrictions are becoming a significant barrier to their adoption.”
Internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare allows website owners to manage AI traffic. For new domains, its settings block agent and training traffic on pages displaying ads.
Eves founded Unlimit in 2009 and built it into a global payments company. Unlimit said in December 2025 that it served more than 50,000 businesses worldwide.
Related: Cloudflare introduces wallets for AI agents, plans stablecoin payments
How smartphone users earn PHASE
Smartphone users can join the Phase network through the Phase app and earn PHASE tokens by validating blocks and sharing their internet connection through the proxy service.
“Current flagship smartphones can deliver approximately 35–45 TOPS [trillions of operations per second] of AI processing performance, depending on the device, allowing them to run smaller open-weight AI models locally,” Eves said.
Related: Tech chief says EU can fend off rogue AI risk: Report
Participation is adjusted based on a device’s battery level and connectivity.
Phase plans AI computing services in November
Smartphone users will be able to contribute computing power when Phase launches its AI computing service, planned for November. A second service expected in November will route requests across AI models.
Phase said that it plans to develop its own model and expand to desktops, servers and graphics processing units.
Part of the revenue from these services would fund PHASE purchases on the open market, which would be used to reward node operators.

articles.title: Treasury Sanctions 11 Over North Korean IT Worker Scheme That Moved Millions in Crypto - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity over North Korean IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and fund the country's weapons programs.
- Treasury says Russian nationals Ilya Boykov and Vitold Obertas converted millions of dollars in crypto for North Korean networks since 2024.
- The sanctions listings include Ethereum and Tron addresses, one of which is linked to both Russian men.
The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in North Korean IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the country's weapons programs, the department said on Wednesday.
North Korea uses fake documents, stolen identities and invented personas to place IT workers at legitimate companies, then takes most of their wages, generating hundreds of millions of dollars for its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs, according to Treasury. The networks have used "sophisticated cryptocurrency transactions," money laundering and artificial intelligence tools to move millions of dollars to the regime, it said.
Today, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK’s unlawful weapons of mass…
— Treasury Department (@USTreasury) October 28, 2026
"The North Korean regime continues targeting and exploiting American companies through fraudulent activities conducted by its overseas IT operatives, who weaponize sensitive data and extort businesses for substantial payments," said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
Two Russian nationals are among those sanctioned. Vitold Obertas, a Russian intermediary for North Korean financial transactions, has carried out nearly $2 million in crypto conversions since January 2025, plus at least $1.25 million in other currency transactions, for North Korean officials, Treasury said. Ilya Boykov has exchanged and converted the equivalent of $3.5 million in crypto since 2024 for Limited Liability Company Alis, a North Korean IT worker company sanctioned in 2024.
The sanctions listings include two Ethereum and two Tron addresses for Boykov, and one Ethereum and three Tron addresses for Obertas. One Ethereum address appears on both men's entries.
Treasury also sanctioned the First Financial and Technical Development Center, a North Korean-controlled entity based in Vladivostok, Russia, that it said deploys highly trained IT workers who use AI tools and "complex cryptocurrency transfers" to generate revenue. Six Russia-based North Korean IT workers have generated more than $750,000 for the center since 2025, according to Treasury.
Two North Korean nationals who lead Russia-based IT worker delegations were also sanctioned. One of them, Kim Ki Hyok, has transferred nearly $500,000 in crypto for his delegation since 2024, Treasury said.
The action builds on sanctions against a separate North Korean IT worker network in March, and Australia and the European Union have made their own designations this month, according to Treasury.
North Korea's crypto operations
North Korean IT workers have increasingly targeted crypto projects. In April 2025, Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that such workers had embedded themselves in crypto projects in the UK, Germany, Portugal and Serbia, including Solana smart contract development, with some operating under as many as 12 fake identities at once.
North Korean hackers have also used long-running deception campaigns against crypto firms. In April, Solana-based exchange Drift Protocol said the attack that drained about $285 million from its platform was a six-month operation by a North Korean state-affiliated group, whose intermediaries met Drift contributors in person and posed as a quantitative trading firm, Decrypt reported.

articles.title: HTX Settles FCA Case Over Unlawful UK Crypto Promotions
articles.text:
HTX agrees to halt unlawful UK crypto promotions after FCA case
HTX has pledged to stop crypto marketing in the UK until October 2031, with deposits and new account registrations already blocked there.
Update (Oct. 29, 2026 at 13:30 UTC): This article has been updated to include HTX’s UK exit and withdrawal arrangements and background on Justin Sun.
Cryptocurrency exchange HTX has agreed to stop unlawfully promoting its services to consumers in the United Kingdom under a settlement announced Thursday by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
Huobi Global S.A., the Panamanian company behind HTX, agreed that it would not knowingly run illegal promotions, including through the exchange’s website, apps or social media. The court undertakings run until Oct. 21, 2031.
The settlement terms are confidential, and the agreement does not constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing.
“Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law,” said Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA. “The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences.”
In an Oct. 16 notice outlining its UK exit arrangements, the exchange formerly known as Huobi said existing UK accounts could no longer deposit or trade. Eligible users can request a one-time 48-hour window to withdraw remaining assets, subject to approval and compliance checks. Accounts will close after all assets have been withdrawn.
The FCA brought the case in October 2025 and announced it in February, which it said was the agency’s first enforcement action against a crypto firm over illegal marketing.
HTX’s Sun ties and sanctions history
HTX counts Tron founder Justin Sun as an adviser. Sun has invested in crypto projects linked to US President Donald Trump, including World Liberty Financial and the TRUMP memecoin.
Sun sued World Liberty in April over the freezing of his WLFI tokens. The company filed a defamation suit against him in May, with Sun denying its allegations.
The settlement in the UK follows separate sanctions against the exchange in the country and European Union.
The UK sanctioned Huobi Global on May 26, imposing an asset freeze over suspected support for Russia’s government. HTX said the company was separate from the exchange, but UK authorities said the platform was covered because Huobi Global owned it.
The EU followed on July 23, imposing a transaction ban on HTX that took effect on Aug. 23.

articles.title: Silicon Valley shifts AI funding to crypto using an Ethereum ICO blueprint
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Y Combinator seeks startups using blockchain to ease AI capital raising, alongside stablecoin banking, trading and agent infrastructure.
- The October request builds on YC's 2025 onchain agenda, which already included capital formation and financial applications for agents.
- YC's on-time Winter 2027 application deadline is November 2 at 8pm Pacific, with late applications still considered.
Y Combinator wants to fund crypto startups that make AI fundraising easier, expand stablecoin banking, and build financial tools for agents, according to its October request for founders.
Visiting partner Nemil Dalal shared the call on Oct. 28, saying YC wanted to fund more crypto companies solving financial needs. Its October Crypto Request for Startups sets out its funding interests for the next six months, spanning capital raising, stablecoins, trading and agents.
The AI capital-raising request connects AI businesses' financing needs with crypto's fundraising history. YC describes investment in AI as one of the largest capital-raising events in human history and points to Ethereum's initial coin offering as a precedent for blockchain fundraising, asking founders to make AI capital raising easier, leaving the financing structure open.
YC and Coinbase's Sept. 23, 2025 request already sought stablecoins, tokenization, trading, on-chain capital formation and apps and agents. The October document gives AI capital raising an explicit place within that continuing financing agenda.
Stablecoins, crypto trading and agent access
YC wants dollar stablecoin products that reach new customer or merchant groups, stablecoins in additional currencies, and neobanks serving people or businesses that existing providers underserve.
Global contractors and international businesses are examples of banking services. The document also points to gaming as a possible customer segment for dollar stablecoins, pairing the choice of user with the need for a distribution strategy.
Distribution is an explicit part of the dollar-stablecoin request: founders must identify a group that benefits from the product and work out how to reach it. The neobank category adds a requirement to manage risk effectively while providing banking services to an underserved segment.
The accelerator asks founders to choose assets that benefit from global, round-the-clock markets and integration with decentralized finance. A house represented by an NFT, with blockchain-based capital helping fund mortgages, appears as an illustrative possibility.
The document also seeks exchanges and interfaces built around new assets, derivatives, or geographies.
YC's broader thesis expects new assets to be issued, including startup equity and small securities, with trading, lending, and derivatives services developing around them.
That expectation connects the fundraising request to the trading categories: the accelerator sees opportunities in both creating assets and building the financial services that make them usable.
Alongside those venues, YC wants founders to build trading applications and infrastructure for agents. The document expects these software actors to become active financial participants and prolific traders, including when a human directs them.
The API category focuses on financial connections designed for agents. YC argues that today's interfaces largely serve human developers, while some agent tasks will require several services to work together.
The infrastructure request recognizes that blockchain access alone may cover only part of an agent's task. YC wants founders to connect the services needed to complete it, including fiat-to-crypto routes.
Its trading request covers activity in crypto and other assets, with agents acting under human instructions and participating more broadly in financial markets.
YC argues that institutional financial needs drove crypto uptake over the past year, citing oil hedging and faster cross-border movement of enterprise money.
For founders responding now, YC's application page lists the Winter 2027 batch as running from January through March in San Francisco. YC will still consider applications submitted after Nov. 2, although it cannot promise when those applicants will receive a response.

articles.title: Utah Files Felony Charges Against Kalshi, Co-Founders Over Sports Bets - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Utah has filed felony charges against Kalshi and co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, accusing them of illegally promoting gambling in the state.
- Prosecutors say an undercover state agent placed 12 sports wagers on Kalshi in September, despite a federal ruling that Utah's gambling laws apply to the platform.
- Kalshi called the charges "a crazy overreach," a day after the CFTC sued Utah to stop it from enforcing its gambling laws against federally regulated exchanges.
Utah has filed criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and its two co-founders, accusing them of illegally promoting gambling in the state, ABC4 reported on Wednesday.
KalshiEX LLC, CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara face one count of pattern of unlawful activity, a second-degree felony, 12 counts of online gambling promotion, a third-degree felony, and one count of gambling promotion, a misdemeanor, according to the charging documents.
"Gambling is illegal in Utah, whether you place the bet, run the game, or promote it. Calling it a 'prediction market' doesn't change what it is, and being federally registered doesn't put a company above the law," Utah Attorney General Derek Brown said in a statement.
According to the charges, a special agent with the Utah State Bureau of Investigation set up an undercover account as a Utah resident and placed 12 wagers on sports including NFL and college games in September, passing a location check that confirmed he was in the state. Kalshi earned proceeds from the fees it charged on each bet, prosecutors allege.
Brown's office did not say what penalties it would seek, though the felony charges carry the possibility of jail time, the Associated Press reported.
"This is a crazy overreach; Utah is clearly playing politics," Kalshi said in a statement. "We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona."
Utah's fight with the CFTC
The charges escalate a dispute that already involves the federal government. Utah, where the state constitution bans gambling, sued Kalshi in state court last week. On Tuesday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah to block its enforcement actions against CFTC-registered exchanges, making it the 10th state the agency has taken to court.
"Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets," CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said.
Utah has already won one round. In August, U.S. District Judge Robert Shelby rejected Kalshi's own bid to block enforcement, ruling that federal law "does not preempt Utah's ability to enforce its anti-gambling laws." Kalshi is appealing to the Tenth Circuit, which denied its request for an injunction in September.
President Donald Trump has backed the CFTC, saying in May that it was "critically important that the CFTC's exclusive authority over Prediction Markets is maintained," and calling several state officials who had challenged the platforms "scum."
Federal appeals courts have split on whether states can apply gambling laws to prediction markets. The Third Circuit ruled in April that New Jersey cannot regulate sports contracts on the platforms, while the Sixth and Ninth Circuits sided with Ohio, Tennessee and Nevada in August and September. New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to settle the question, backed by 39 other states and the District of Columbia.
"Different judges in different places say different things," Isaac Rose-Berman, a gambling policy fellow at the American Institute for Boys and Men, told ABC4. "It's just going to keep escalating and eventually get to the Supreme Court."

articles.title: EU Investors Rank Crypto Above Pensions as Lasting Wealth Tools: OKX Survey
articles.text:
EU investors rank crypto above retirement plans for lasting wealth creation: OKX survey
European investors ranked crypto above retirement plans for lasting wealth creation, while prior surveys show US investors are skeptical on crypto’s role in retirement accounts.
Investors in several of Europe’s biggest economies ranked crypto above retirement plans as lasting wealth creation tools, with 19% of those surveyed choosing cryptocurrencies, while 8% opted for traditional retirement plans.
US investors still preferred traditional retirement plans, with 21% choosing retirement accounts while only 12% opted for cryptocurrencies, according to a Thursday OKX survey of 1,932 adults age 18 to 88 who previously invested in crypto. The survey was conducted by Pollfish between Oct. 14 and Oct. 18 across the US, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Poland.
Real estate was the top choice for lasting wealth, with 34% of all respondents choosing the broad class above digital assets and retirement accounts, as the asset most associated with lasting wealth.
Younger Europeans have previously shown concerns about whether their retirement plans will provide sufficient income. About 43% of 2,000 surveyed Europeans age 18 to 35 expected their pensions to fall short, according to a May 2026 survey by Friends of Europe’s citizen-engagement unit, Debating Europe.
“When investors under 45 on both sides of the Atlantic treat crypto as part of their long-term wealth, it tells you crypto is now part of how people look at their finances,” said OKX Europe’s CEO, Erald Ghoo. He said that crypto’s place in the wealth plan will become “more important” as these investors get older and wealthier.
Over half of US investors plan to increase their crypto holdings, while boomers remain skeptical
Nearly half of European investors, 47%, expect to increase their holdings, including 13% planning a significant increase. Across all age groups, 51% expect to increase their crypto allocation. Boomers are the exception, with 55% saying crypto is not important to generational wealth.
Excluding boomers, US investors generally are more bullish on cryptocurrency’s place in their portfolio, with 55% of surveyed participants expecting to increase their allocation in the next five years and 22% planning a significant increase.
Still, American boomers were more pessimistic about crypto, with 65% saying that crypto was not at all important for generational wealth building, compared to 44% of boomers in Europe.
Related: Settlement concerns prompt Euronext to halt CoinShares’ Zcash ETP ahead of debut
Trump administration broadens retirement plan access to alternative assets
To be sure, Americans are also more skeptical about crypto’s place in retirement accounts. An August survey from The National Institute on Retirement Security found that 77% of Americans consider crypto in workplace retirement plans risky, including 46% who view it as very risky.
Earlier, however, the Trump administration took steps toward broadening access to alternative assets in retirement plans. In May 2025, the US Department of Labor rescinded crypto-specific guidance that had urged 401(k) plan fiduciaries to exercise “extreme care” when considering cryptocurrency investments, returning instead to a neutral approach that neither endorses nor discourages crypto.
In August 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to expand access to alternative assets in 401(k) plans, including exposure to digital assets through certain investment vehicles.
In March 2026, the US Department of Labor issued a draft proposal seeking to expand investment options in 401(k) retirement plans to include crypto and alternative investments.
In June 2026, SenatorsBernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren and Representative Bobby Scott urged the US Department of Labor to withdraw its proposal to allow digital assets in retirement plans, arguing that the policy would “expose retirement accounts to exceptionally volatile assets, like digital currency.”

articles.title: Trump's crypto firm joins Tether, Circle, and Ripple in $2.6 billion stablecoin freeze as Binance hack outflows near $6 billion
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Stablecoin issuers have frozen over $2.6 billion as Binance investigated a suspected hack involving $5.8 billion in cryptocurrency transfers.
- Researchers traced suspicious transactions across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron blockchain networks.
- About $850 million in ETH was reportedly still moving between wallets, raising questions about how much of the suspected stolen assets can be recovered.
Stablecoin issuers, including Tether, Circle, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial, have frozen more than $2.6 billion in digital assets linked to a suspected Binance security breach involving nearly $6 billion.
On Oct. 29, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $ 1.567 billion in USDT linked to the suspected incident. He wrote on X:
“Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority.”
Circle also froze approximately $823 million in USDC linked to the incident. CEO Jeremy Allaire confirmed that the company was coordinating with law enforcement to restrict the movement of potentially compromised assets and support the investigation.
Other stablecoin issuers joined the effort, with Ripple reportedly freezing approximately $200 million and Donald Trump-linked World Liberty Financial restricting $27 million in USD1.
Paxos also disclosed that it had frozen 1,906.67 PAX Gold (PAXG) tokens valued at more than $8 million.
Together, the reported freezes exceed $2.6 billion, representing a substantial portion of the approximately $6 billion in assets reportedly transferred from Binance-linked wallets.
However, Binance has not yet confirmed the total amount potentially compromised, leaving the scale of the suspected breach unresolved.
Binance hack outflows approach $6 billion
Crypto research firm Kairos Research estimated that about $5.7 billion left Binance hot wallets. According to the firm, the suspicious activity began at 4:20 p.m. ET when an external address used Ethereum's EIP-7702 account-delegation mechanism to attach executable code to a Binance hot wallet.
Three minutes later, a single transaction transferred 63 tokens, including 1.6 billion USDT and 167,000 ETH.
Another Binance hot wallet transferred 28,000 ETH to the same destination, while 18,270 BTC and 613 million USDT on Tron moved to new addresses around the same time.
The research firm said the attacker kept moving assets after the initial freezes, including another 200 million USDT transferred through the compromised Ethereum wallet, which was later frozen.
Before Tether intervened, the suspected attacker also deposited $60 million in USDT into Aave and borrowed about 19,800 ETH, valued at $45 million.
Kairos reported that Aave subsequently paused most of its Ethereum lending markets, restricting new deposits and borrowing activity. Aave said on X:
“Aave’s contracts are unaffected, and positions remain overcollateralized. As a precaution, all DAO-operated markets across V3 and V4 have been frozen. The freeze pauses new deposits and borrows, and users can still withdraw and repay their existing positions.”
Despite these measures, approximately $850 million in ETH continued moving between newly created wallets, while 17,270 BTC remained untouched.
Meanwhile, Binance confirmed that its security teams were investigating the suspicious activity and reviewing available information. The exchange also assured customers their assets were safe and promised further updates once it verified the circumstances.

articles.title: Coinbase Files for Brazil Crypto License Ahead of Deadline
articles.text:
Coinbase seeks Brazil crypto license, expects no service disruption
Coinbase has applied for authorization ahead of Brazil’s Oct. 30 deadline and says it expects to maintain existing services while regulators review its application.
Coinbase has applied for authorization to operate as a crypto service provider in Brazil ahead of the country’s license application deadline on Friday.
The US-based cryptocurrency exchange submitted its application to the Central Bank of Brazil on Wednesday under the country’s virtual asset service provider (VASP) framework, according to a statement shared with Cointelegraph.
The filing aims to maintain Coinbase’s existing Brazilian operations as the central bank introduces new requirements covering governance, customer asset safeguards and compliance.
“We do not expect the application review to require a suspension of our existing services,” a Coinbase spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Coinbase also reiterated plans to bring its “Everything Exchange” strategy to Brazil, potentially expanding into foreign exchange and payments alongside crypto services. Those activities require separate regulatory authorizations.
Coinbase joins Binance, which applied for authorization on Oct. 23 but has restricted crypto lending, margin trading and other services in Brazil while delisting 22 crypto assets to comply with the new rules.
Brazil requires existing crypto service providers to apply for authorization by the end of October to continue operating under transitional arrangements. Existing providers that apply by the deadline can continue operating while their applications are reviewed.
Related: France proposes liability for crypto exchanges offering DeFi access

articles.title: The Fed's rate freeze will mean nothing unless banks fix a repo market bottleneck
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The Fed held its target range at 3.75%-4% on Oct. 28, with operating instructions effective the following day.
- Reserve interest is 3.9%, standing repo 4% and reverse repo 3.75%, serving different roles in short-term rate control.
- The directive conditionally permits short-Treasury purchases to maintain ample reserves, with no announced amount or reported execution.
The Federal Reserve held its rate target range at 3.75%-4% on Oct. 28, with operating instructions effective the following day setting out how to implement that stance across bank reserves and overnight funding markets.
The Federal Open Market Committee's October decision passed 10-2, with Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack dissenting and preferring a quarter-percentage-point increase.
The Oct. 29 accompanying implementation note maintains interest on reserve balances (IORB) at 3.9%, with standing overnight repo at 4% and reverse repo offered at 3.75%.
The 3.75%-4% range is the FOMC's policy target for the federal funds market, where banks and other eligible entities borrow and lend balances held at the Fed overnight without collateral.
As the New York Fed explains, administered rates help keep that market rate within the target range. An instruction to maintain the range differs from a report of where transactions cleared.
The Federal Reserve Board sets the interest paid on eligible institutions' reserve balances at the Fed. Its IORB guidance describes the payment as a tool for implementing monetary policy and controlling short-term rates.
At the directive's 4% rate, standing overnight repo offers secured overnight funding. In a repo, the New York Fed's trading desk buys securities with an agreement to resell them. The transaction temporarily adds reserves and helps limit upward pressure on money-market rates.
Overnight reverse repo works in the opposite direction, as the Desk sells securities with an agreement to buy them back, temporarily reducing reserves. The New York Fed's repo and reverse repo explanation describes the two tools as supporting rate control and smooth market functioning.
The reverse repo terms also include a $160 billion daily limit per counterparty.
Conditional purchases and the relation with rates
The directive permits the Desk, when appropriate, to increase the System Open Market Account's holdings through Treasury-bill purchases to maintain ample reserves. If needed, it can also buy other Treasury securities with no more than three years remaining to maturity.
The note also directs the Desk to roll over all principal payments from Treasury holdings at auction and reinvest all principal payments from agency securities into Treasury bills.
The practical lesson for crypto markets is to distinguish the chosen interest-rate stance from the operations that maintain it. The October package describes a hold implemented through an ample-reserves system.
Transaction results and purchase records would show how the instructions are executed. Separate evidence of crypto demand and transmission would be needed to connect those operations to Bitcoin.

articles.title: RootstockLabs Sees New Financial Role for Bitcoin
articles.text:
Bitcoin lending and yield could drive next wave of institutional demand, Rootstock says
A new report argues that putting institutional Bitcoin holdings to work through lending, collateral and financing could create demand beyond its store-of-value role.
A new report from Bitcoin infrastructure developer RootstockLabs argues that Bitcoin’s next wave of institutional demand could come from lending, yield generation and balance-sheet financing, expanding its role beyond a store of value.
RootstockLabs estimates that just 1.5% of Bitcoin’s (BTC) supply currently participates in lending and Bitcoin-native finance, while identifiable institutional investors hold roughly 3.9 million BTC. Putting more of those holdings to work could create additional demand for the asset without changing its fixed supply.
The analysis identifies two emerging sources of financial utility: generating returns from existing Bitcoin holdings through lending and structured credit, and using Bitcoin alongside fiat-denominated liabilities to improve corporate balance-sheet efficiency. RootstockLabs argues that both could encourage institutions to acquire and retain more BTC.
Bitcoin’s evolving financial utility compared with traditional assets. Source: RootstockLabs report
The report outlines a hypothetical scenario in which institutional Bitcoin holdings double to 7.8 million BTC. If 5% of those holdings earned a 5% annual yield, institutions would collectively generate 19,500 BTC a year. The figure represents potential returns on existing holdings, not a forecast of new Bitcoin demand.
Drawing a comparison to gold, the report argues that successful monetary assets develop additional sources of demand beyond their original role as stores of value. While gold found uses in jewelry and electronics, RootstockLabs sees Bitcoin’s next source of utility emerging through financial markets.
Related: Bitcoin ETF inflows climb to $176M as BTC rebounds above $80K
Could Bitcoin’s financialization introduce new risks?
Asked about the risks associated with Bitcoin’s growing financialization, Tony DiCarlo, director of institutional propositions at RootstockLabs and author of the report, acknowledged the concerns but argued that Bitcoin’s underlying design offers important advantages. He told Cointelegraph:
Yes, financialisation carries real risks. Fractional reserves, rehypothecation and excess leverage can grow around any scarce asset. Bitcoin’s traits reduce some of that risk as collateral is verifiable on-chain, liquidation rules are programmable and the supply of collateral cannot be diluted.
DiCarlo said borrower defaults, custody failures and legal enforceability remain concerns, while Bitcoin’s volatility adds to leverage risks.
However, he argued that the benefits of financialization could far outweigh those risks, pointing to MARA’s $750 million in Bitcoin-backed loans to help finance a planned power plant acquisition in Ohio. The arrangement allows MARA to retain its Bitcoin holdings while using them as collateral to finance real-world infrastructure.
Bitcoin’s key features for modern finance. Source: RootstockLabs report
DiCarlo also acknowledged that institutional adoption could concentrate Bitcoin holdings among a small number of custodians. While spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have been a major driver of institutional adoption, “shareholders own shares, not coins,” he said, warning that a few large custodians could end up holding most of the Bitcoin.
Nevertheless, DiCarlo maintained that Bitcoin’s decentralized architecture remains a fundamental advantage, allowing holders to retain control of their assets and enabling financial services with fewer intermediaries, potentially reducing counterparty risks and fees.
Bitcoin’s defining trait is that nobody owns it and you don’t need an intermediary to use it. Holders keep control of their keys and because there are fewer middlemen, financial services built on Bitcoin can carry less counterparty risk and fewer fees. Those advantages draw users in and they reward the builders who design around them.
Magazine: Crypto could outperform AI stocks: Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser

articles.title: Bitcoin whipsaws below $79,000 as Binance hot wallet reportedly drained by Tornado Cash-linked wallet
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Binance is investigating a potential security issue after large transfers left labeled wallets.
- Tether froze about $1.57B and Circle froze $823M tied to the suspected incident.
- Bitcoin fell to $78,297 as nearly $1B in crypto liquidations hit over 24 hours.
Bitcoin hit an intraday low of $78,297 on Binance spot on Oct. 29 and sat near $79,126 at press time, as large transfers left Binance-labeled wallets.
Binance shared on X that the exchange is “aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.”
It added:
“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.”
Former CEO Changpeng Zhao went further on X, arguing that “it does look like a hack on Binance.”
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino confirmed that the firm froze roughly $1.57 billion related to the potential hack, while Circle froze about $823 million.
What the chain shows
Whale Alert recorded 28,005 ETH, about $64.9 million, leaving a Binance-labeled wallet at 20:24:47 UTC, and 780 million USDC leaving another at 20:41:23 UTC. Both went to the same new address.
At 20:38:47 UTC, the receiving address forwarded 195,460 ETH, about $449 million, to a second address.
On-chain watchers circulated a total close to $2.8 billion across five chains, and the full figure remains unreconciled.
Analyst Spreek first flagged the activity, noting that the contract call behind it was funded by an address linked to Tornado Cash.
DefiLlama co-founder 0xngmi argued that Binance has $144 billion in assets under custody and that the amount effectively stolen would represent less than 1% of that value, so the exchange could “cover it from balance sheet easily.”
The Bitcoin selloff began earlier
Bitcoin was already weak before the first highlighted transfer, having traded below $80,000 earlier on Oct. 29 as a technology-stock selloff and a hawkish reading of the Fed's Oct. 28 hold weighed on risk assets.
Binance spot data shows Bitcoin sliding from about $80,849 to $80,438 between 20:00 and 20:15 UTC. The 20:30 to 20:45 candle closed at $78,884.52, down about 1.9%, and the low came in the next quarter hour.
CoinGlass reported nearly $1 billion in liquidations in the past 24 hours, and roughly $532 million in liquidations in the past hour. Bitcoin liquidations totaled $289 million, and Ethereum's totaled $236 million.

articles.title: Bitcoin Faces Sell-Side Risk Above $85,000, Glassnode Analysis Warns
articles.text:
Bitcoin long-term resistance in focus as analysis sees selling risk above $85K
BTC price analysis from Glassnode drew attention to $85,000 as the lower boundary of a cost-basis zone for long-term holders.
Bitcoin (BTC) faces resistance between $84,000 and $85,000 as analysis points to coins largely linked to a single large holder.
Key points:
- Bitcoin faces resistance around $85,000, where 4.3% of the BTC supply last moved onchain.
- Glassnode analysis links the onchain cost basis of 864,520 BTC to Bitcoin’s difficulty sustaining daily closes above $85,000.
- Long-term holders own a combined four million coins with a cost basis between $85,000 and $118,000.
Glassnode ties $85K resistance to large-holder cost basis
In the latest edition of its regular newsletter, The Week Onchain, crypto analytics platform Glassnode flagged another resistance hurdle for BTC price action in the mid-$80,000 range.
On Nov. 22, 2025, a significant portion of the total BTC supply moved onchain. At the time of the transactions, BTC/USD traded between $84,000 and $85,000. The coins that last moved at that price make up 4.3% of the total BTC supply, or 864,520 BTC.
The analysis links the majority of this Bitcoin to a single large holder, who was moving funds among multiple wallets. Although self-transfers generally do not affect price, Glassnode noted that Bitcoin has respected the $84,000-$85,000 range as both support and resistance over the past 11 months.
“It held as support in December, when price bounced off it on December 1 and December 18. It gave way on January 31, when a push back up to $84K failed, and Bitcoin fell about 20% over the following days,” Glassnode commented.
In May, September and October, BTC price upside momentum faded near the same level, with a high of $87,400. Bitcoin has recorded only five daily closes above the band, never more than three in a row.
“A run of daily closes above $85K would turn the band back into support,” Glassnode added.
BTC/USD chart with supply onchain cost-basis data. Source: Glassnode
Long-term holders pose sell-side risk above $85,000
The $85,000 mark holds significance for a larger portion of the Bitcoin investor base.
Related: Bitcoin price analysis sees ‘strong rally’ as old coins become dormant
Glassnode reports that Bitcoin’s long-term holders (LTH) — entities holding a given amount of BTC without selling for at least 155 days — own around 4 million coins that last moved onchain between $85,000 and $118,000, mostly in 2025.
“More than half of all their coins were bought above today’s price. If price recovers toward $85K, many of these holders may sell to get their money back,” it said of the LTH cohort as a whole.
Bitcoin supply data by investor cohort. Source: Glassnode
The LTH spent output profit ratio (SOPR), which compares the extent to which LTH coins moving onchain are doing so at a higher or lower price compared to their previous transaction, currently sits at 0.99. Values below 1 imply that LTH supply is moving at an aggregate loss.

articles.title: Kalshi’s Senate contracts can settle on different answers to the same election
articles.text:
Quick Take
- An Oct. 28 Kalshi snapshot priced four Senate contracts at $3.02 before fees, exceeding their conditional $3 gross payout.
- Control can resolve early on media calls, while seat contracts use February composition, exposing the hedge to different settlement outcomes.
- Displayed depth, fees and collateral-return settings affect execution and the cash committed to the four positions.
Prediction exchange Kalshi’s Senate markets showed different Democratic odds on Oct. 28, but buying a four-contract hedge at the quoted prices cost $3.02 before fees for a $3 gross payout only if the control and seat-count outcomes aligned.
The Senate-control market had a 64.5% midpoint at 22:11:45 UTC, while a normalized estimate from the Democratic seat-count markets put the chance of 51 or more seats at about 62.1%. That 2.4-percentage-point gap was a comparison between prices. The four purchase quotes already exceeded the conditional payout by two cents, and the contracts’ different settlement provisions left a separate risk.
The quote test comes alongside Talos’s Oct. 28 research into pricing differences across Senate markets. Its historical nine-leg model found occasional positive results under stated execution assumptions. The four-leg calculation here examines a separate package using purchase quotes captured on Oct. 28.
What the $3.02 package buys
The package combines one YES on Democratic Senate control with one NO on each of three disjoint seat outcomes: exactly 51, exactly 52 and above 52. Those seat buckets cover every Democratic total of 51 or more without overlapping.
At the Oct. 28 snapshot, the purchase prices were:
| Position | Quoted purchase price | 
|---|---|
| Democratic Senate control: YES | $0.65 | 
| Exactly 51 Democratic seats: NO | $0.9 | 
| Exactly 52 Democratic seats: NO | $0.84 | 
| Above 52 Democratic seats: NO | $0.63 | 
| Total for one of each | $3.02 before fees | 
If Democratic control resolves YES and Democrats finish in one of those seat buckets, the control contract pays $1. Two of the three seat-NO contracts pay $1 each, while the third pays nothing. The total is $3.
If control resolves NO and Democrats finish below 51 seats, all three seat-NO contracts pay and the control YES pays nothing. That also totals $3. Both aligned cases leave a two-cent loss before fees at the quoted purchase prices. No orders were executed.
The midpoint comparison answers a different question. A midpoint is halfway between the price offered by a buyer and the price requested by a seller. The three 51-plus bucket midpoints themselves summed to 64.5%, matching the control midpoint. All seat buckets together summed to 103.8%; rescaling that full ladder to 100% produced the 62.1% estimate. Buying the hedge still requires paying each seller’s quoted ask.
Even a purchase below $3 would need another test: whether the four legs actually offset.
Kalshi’s CONTROL terms permit accelerated resolution when at least four of eight designated media sources declare a winner and none issues a contradictory declaration. Kalshi retains discretion over accelerated resolution. The current market rules otherwise use the party of the Senate’s president pro tempore on Feb. 1, 2027.
The seat-count terms use Senate composition on Feb. 1, with a fallback to the next date data becomes available, and count independents with the party they caucus with. The seat outcome therefore rests on composition at a later observation date than a possible early control call.
A vacancy, caucus change or altered race outcome between a control determination and the composition date could separate the results.
The cash consequences run both ways. If control YES wins but Democrats fall outside the 51-plus buckets, all four contracts pay, totaling $4. If control YES loses but Democrats end up in a 51-plus bucket, only two seat-NO contracts pay, totaling $2.
A trader retains exposure to the difference between an early control determination and later chamber composition, even after completing all four positions.
Displayed depth, fees and tied-up capital
A later set of orderbook snapshots, retrieved sequentially at 22:16:13 UTC, still implied the same four purchase prices. The displayed quantities were uneven: 363.87 contracts for control YES, compared with 75,698.05 for NO on 51, 21,942.19 for NO on 52 and 17,253.28 for NO above 52.
The control leg limited the size visible at those best prices. Buying 1,000 equal packages would require reaching deeper into that book, even though the three seat legs displayed much more quantity. The requests captured separate books in sequence, and displayed orders could change before all four legs filled.
Kalshi’s orderbook documentation explains the price relationship: the books list YES and NO bid quotes, with an ask derived from one dollar minus the opposite bid.
Fees require similar care. Kalshi says some markets have maker fees, so leaving a resting order cannot universally be treated as free execution. The $3.02 purchase total excludes fees. Actual charges depend on the applicable market and order sequence, and any trading charge would add to the loss in the aligned payout cases.
Its rounding documentation also distinguishes direct-member balances, aligned to $0.0001, from non-direct-member balances, aligned to $0.01. Model fees round upward to six decimal dollars, while an order-level accumulator can rebate rounding overpayments across fills.
