articles.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur were Stanford roommates who both studied computer science before spending a decade at Palantir. Elder led product design for a team of 800 people building software for U.S. defense and intelligence agencies, while Mathur served as a senior vice president in the company’s commercial practice. When the friends decided to build a startup early last year, there was no question they would do it together.
Despite having no direct background in architecture, Elder and Mathur were troubled by a growing problem: Fewer buildings are constructed in the U.S. today than a few decades ago, as development costs have surged.
“We’ve gone from dial-up internet to superintelligent AI, but our ability to build the physical world around us has actually decreased,” Mathur told TechCrunch.
Believing AI can boost productivity across the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, they set out to build Dream, a startup developing built world models that automate building design and engineering. Dream has emerged from stealth with $17 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, alongside other backers, including SV Angel, XYZ, and Zigg Capital. The startup aims to replace cumbersome, outdated AEC tools like Autodesk’s AutoCAD and Revit.
If you sit next to an architect or a structural engineer, you’ll notice that they are still “drawing” every piece of their designs part by part on legacy software, Mathur said. “AI really plays no role in that equation.”
While a standard LLM like ChatGPT can generate an image of a building, the result won’t be structurally sound. Dream, by contrast, is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream’s world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.
“Our model actually understands what’s within those walls. What materials are used, what the beams are made of, and how much weight they can support,” Elder said.
The startup calls its approach “structural cognition” because its model generates structurally precise designs that account for internal building elements like plumbing and HVAC.
Dream has already begun selling its product to AEC professionals and developers, who use the model to conceptualize building designs and estimate overall costs, according to the founders. The platform is already deployed across 10 active projects in Texas and California.
While Dream isn’t the only company attempting to update AEC software with AI — other startups working on this include Motif, Snaptrude, and Arcol — Elder and Mathur claim that they are the only ones that developed a world model that instantly designs whole buildings.
Kimberly Tan, a partner at Andreessen Horowitz, said that while the firm first invested in Dream over a year ago, when the startup model was just an idea, she has been extremely impressed with their progress. “I have not seen anybody take the technical approach,” she said. “They’re doing everything based on their own models.”

articles.title: Giá lợn hơi giảm xuống đáy, siêu thị có loại vẫn bán 280.000 đồng/kg
articles.text:
Giá lợn hơi giảm sâu, người tiêu dùng vẫn phải mua giá đắt
Trao đổi với PV VietNamNet sáng 28/10, anh Trần Thảo - chủ một trang trại chăn nuôi ở xã Bảo Thắng (Lào Cai) nói: “Giá lợn hơi hôm nay đã ngừng giảm, giữ ở mức 42.000-44.000 đồng/kg. Hy vọng đây là giá đáy”.
Anh Thảo cho biết, với mức giá hiện tại, ngay cả những trang trại chăn nuôi chủ động được con giống cũng lỗ khoảng 800.000 đồng khi xuất bán một con lợn thịt trọng lượng 120-130kg.
Đây là mức lỗ anh tính toán dựa trên các chỉ số chăn nuôi đạt hiệu quả tốt, giá thành sản xuất từ 49.000-50.000 đồng/kg lợn hơi. Còn với những hộ dân chăn nuôi có tỷ lệ thất thoát cao, cộng với việc phải mua con giống còn lỗ nặng hơn.
“Năm nay chăn nuôi khó khăn, giá lợn hơi có xu hướng giảm sâu, trong khi giá cám từ đầu năm đến nay đã tăng 3.000 đồng/kg, dự kiến từ nay đến cuối năm còn tăng thêm 2-3 đợt nữa”, anh nói.
Bình thường, quy mô nuôi ở trang trại của anh luôn duy trì khoảng 1.000 con lợn, nhưng dịp này sau khi xuất bán, anh Thảo tạm thời “treo chuồng”.
Chị Nguyễn Thị Hương, đầu mối thu mua lợn thương phẩm tại xã Lập Thạch (Phú Thọ), cho biết hơn một tuần nay, giá lợn hơi giảm khá sâu. Ngày 28/10, giá lợn hơi loại ngon, nhiều nạc chỉ 46.000 đồng/kg. Còn với loại lợn nhiều mỡ, quá trọng lượng thì giá chỉ còn 40.000 đồng/kg.
Theo chị, sức tiêu thụ không tăng trong khi nguồn cung lại dồi dào, lợn quá trọng lượng nhiều nên người nuôi buộc phải bán giá thấp để cắt lỗ.
Hiện giá lợn hơi trung bình phổ biến ở mức 44.000-48.000 đồng/kg, tùy nơi. Đây là mức giá thấp nhất kể từ đầu năm.
Trái ngược với giá lợn hơi xuất chuồng, tại chợ và siêu thị ở Hà Nội, thịt lợn vẫn có giá bán khá cao. Đơn cử, tại một số hệ thống siêu thị lớn, thịt đùi lợn có giá 138.000 đồng/kg, thịt nạc xay giá 140.000 đồng/kg, chân giò rút xương có giá 174.000 đồng/kg, thịt ba chỉ gần 200.000 đồng/kg.
Sườn thăn là mặt hàng có giá cao nhất, được một hệ thống siêu thị niêm yết ở mức 280.000 đồng/kg.
Tại chợ Đại Từ (Định Công, Hà Nội), thịt ba chỉ, sườn lợn và nạc thăn đều có giá 150.000 đồng/kg; mông sấn 100.000 đồng/kg, thịt chân giò, nạc mông và nạc vai giá dao động từ 120.000-130.000 đồng/kg...
"Dịp này giá đã giảm khoảng 10.000-15.000 đồng/kg do giá lợn hơi xuất chuồng giảm", một tiểu thương tại chợ Đại Từ cho hay, nhưng theo chị sức tiêu thụ mặt hàng này vẫn khá yếu.
Khâu trung gian, bán lẻ 'sáng giao, chiều thu tiền' hưởng lợi lớn
Trao đổi với VietNamNet, giám đốc một doanh nghiệp chăn nuôi quy mô hơn 300.000 con lợn thương phẩm thừa nhận, giá lợn hơi liên tục đi xuống khoảng 2 tháng gần đây. Nguyên nhân do tâm lý e ngại của người tiêu dùng trước thông tin về chất cấm, dịch tả lợn châu Phi và thịt nhập khẩu giá siêu rẻ.
Riêng thịt nhập khẩu, dù chỉ chiếm tỷ trọng nhỏ trong tổng nhu cầu thị trường, chưa đủ để tạo ra biến động lớn về cung - cầu, song giá rất rẻ đã tạo tâm lý so sánh trên thị trường, vị này nhận xét.
Về nguồn cung, việc siết chặt các quy định về môi trường, chất cấm và kiểm soát dịch bệnh khiến một số cơ sở chăn nuôi không đủ điều kiện phải ngừng hoạt động, bán tháo đàn.
Theo ông, nhóm hộ chuyên nuôi gột, mua lợn khoảng 110kg về nuôi tiếp lên 140-150kg cũng giảm hoặc ngừng vào đàn. Trước đây, nhóm này góp phần điều tiết nguồn cung khi giữ lợn thêm 15-20 ngày mới xuất bán. Nay hoạt động nuôi gột thu hẹp, lượng lợn từ các trang trại và lợn nuôi gột cùng được đưa ra thị trường, tạo thêm áp lực giảm giá.
Giá lợn hơi giảm cũng khiến người chăn nuôi hạn chế tái đàn, làm sức tiêu thụ lợn giống đi xuống. Trước áp lực quá tải chuồng nuôi, các đơn vị cung cấp lợn giống buộc phải chuyển sang nuôi thịt và xuất bán sớm để giải phóng diện tích. Một số trang trại cũng chủ động xuất chuồng sớm do lo ngại nguy cơ dịch bệnh, khiến nguồn cung thịt lợn tăng trong thời gian ngắn.
Vị giám đốc doanh nghiệp cho hay, giá lợn hơi hồi đầu tháng 9 vẫn ở mức 59.000-60.000 đồng/kg. Đến nay, doanh nghiệp chỉ bán được với giá 46.000-47.000 đồng/kg tại miền Bắc và 50.000-51.000 đồng/kg tại miền Nam.
Điều đáng nói, giá lợn hơi giảm sâu trong bối cảnh chi phí thức ăn chăn nuôi và các đầu vào khác tăng mạnh khiến người nuôi chịu sức ép lớn. So với cùng mức giá lợn hơi của năm trước, giá thành sản xuất năm nay đã tăng thêm khoảng 4.000-5.000 đồng/kg. Vì vậy, các hộ chăn nuôi nhỏ lẻ khó tránh thua lỗ nặng, còn những đơn vị kiểm soát tốt chi phí cũng bị thu hẹp đáng kể biên lợi nhuận.
Ngoài ra, một bất cập khác hiện nay là giá lợn hơi tại chuồng giảm mạnh nhưng giá thịt bán lẻ ở chợ truyền thống và siêu thị chưa giảm tương ứng.
“Lâu nay, khâu trung gian và bán lẻ không trực tiếp gánh rủi ro sản xuất, chỉ ‘sáng giao, chiều thu tiền’ lại hưởng lợi lớn nhất trong chuỗi giá trị chăn nuôi. Trong khi người nuôi phải chịu chi phí đầu vào và biến động giá, nhiều giai đoạn gánh lỗ nặng”, vị này chỉ rõ.
Để khắc phục tình trạng trên, vị giám đốc cho rằng cơ quan quản lý cần công khai cơ cấu giá từ lợn hơi xuất chuồng đến các loại thịt thành phẩm, giúp người tiêu dùng có căn cứ tham chiếu và tăng tính minh bạch trên thị trường.
Đồng thời, cần làm rõ các khoản chi phí tuân thủ như kiểm dịch, phí vào chợ... bởi chi phí thực tế mà người chăn nuôi và thương lái phải trả được cho là cao hơn mức quy định, làm tăng chi phí trung gian một cách bất hợp lý.
Khi giá thịt bán lẻ giảm phù hợp với diễn biến giá lợn hơi, sức mua có thể được cải thiện, qua đó hỗ trợ thị trường phục hồi.

articles.title: Hậu biến cố Chủ tịch bị khởi tố, DN ngành điện bứt phá nhờ lãi đậm, tiền mặt lớn
articles.text:
Cổ phiếu TV2 tăng trần, lợi nhuận bứt tốc
Trong phiên giao dịch ngày 28/10, cổ phiếu TV2 của CTCP Tư vấn Xây dựng Điện 2 (PECC2) tăng kịch trần 1.800 đồng, lên 27.850 đồng/cổ phiếu, sau khi mở cửa tại mức tham chiếu. Kết phiên, dư mua giá trần còn gần 337.000 đơn vị, trong khi bên bán không còn cổ phiếu chờ khớp.
Đà tăng này nối tiếp nhịp hồi phục của TV2 từ giữa tháng 10, sau giai đoạn điều chỉnh kéo dài. Từng tăng mạnh trong hai tháng đầu năm và đạt đỉnh khoảng 43.000 đồng/cổ phiếu vào đầu tháng 3, thị giá TV2 sau đó liên tục đi xuống, có thời điểm chạm 23.700 đồng/cổ phiếu vào cuối tháng 7, mức thấp nhất trong khoảng ba năm.
Diễn biến tiêu cực diễn ra trong bối cảnh thị trường chịu tác động từ thông tin một số lãnh đạo doanh nghiệp trong lĩnh vực điện bị khởi tố. Tháng 5, TV2 công bố ông Nguyễn Chơn Hùng, Chủ tịch HĐQT cùng bà Bùi Thị Ngọc Lý, Kế toán trưởng bị khởi tố trong quá trình điều tra vụ án xảy ra tại Tổng công ty Truyền tải điện Quốc gia, Tập đoàn PC1 và một số đơn vị liên quan.
Báo cáo kinh doanh quý III/2026 cho thấy lợi nhuận TV2 cải thiện đáng kể, trong bối cảnh cổ phiếu phục hồi từ giữa tháng 10.
Cụ thể, doanh thu thuần trong quý đạt hơn 517 tỷ đồng, gấp hơn hai lần cùng kỳ năm trước. Giá vốn tăng chậm hơn doanh thu giúp lợi nhuận gộp đạt 90 tỷ đồng, tăng khoảng 2,2 lần; biên lợi nhuận gộp cải thiện từ 16% lên 17,5%.
Đáng chú ý, doanh thu hoạt động tài chính tăng vọt lên gần 36 tỷ đồng, so với khoảng 5,5 tỷ đồng cùng kỳ. Dù chi phí tài chính tăng gấp bốn lần, lên gần 8,5 tỷ đồng, cùng chi phí bán hàng và quản lý doanh nghiệp gia tăng, TV2 vẫn ghi nhận lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt 61 tỷ đồng, cao gấp hơn 4,5 lần mức 13,4 tỷ đồng cùng kỳ.
Lũy kế 9 tháng, doanh thu thuần đạt gần 1.200 tỷ đồng, tăng mạnh so với khoảng 770 tỷ đồng cùng kỳ năm ngoái. Lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt hơn 162 tỷ đồng, gấp 3,5 lần mức gần 45,8 tỷ đồng.
So với kế hoạch năm 2026, TV2 hoàn thành chưa tới 50% mục tiêu doanh thu nhưng đã vượt 62% chỉ tiêu lợi nhuận. Kết quả này cho thấy khả năng sinh lời cải thiện rõ rệt, dù tiến độ thực hiện kế hoạch doanh thu vẫn là vấn đề cần theo dõi trong những tháng cuối năm.
Một điểm sáng khác là lượng tiền mặt và tiền gửi ngân hàng tăng mạnh. Riêng 9 tháng đầu năm, doanh thu tài chính đạt gần 100 tỷ đồng, trong đó lãi tiền gửi và cho vay hơn 87 tỷ đồng, gấp khoảng 24 lần cùng kỳ. Nguồn thu này đóng góp đáng kể vào tăng trưởng lợi nhuận của doanh nghiệp.
Tiền mặt tăng mạnh, công nợ và tiền ứng trước ở mức cao
Báo cáo tài chính cuối quý III/2026 cho thấy quy mô tài sản của TV2 mở rộng nhanh chóng. Tổng tài sản đạt hơn 4.800 tỷ đồng, tăng khoảng 62% so với đầu năm. Trong đó, tài sản ngắn hạn đạt gần 3.926 tỷ đồng, tăng mạnh so với hơn 2.110 tỷ đồng hồi đầu năm.
Đáng chú ý, tiền mặt và tiền gửi ngân hàng tăng từ khoảng 1.112 tỷ đồng lên 2.114 tỷ đồng, tương đương gần 1,9 lần. Khoản mục này chiếm khoảng 44% tổng tài sản, tạo vùng đệm thanh khoản đáng kể và giúp doanh nghiệp có nguồn lực để đáp ứng nhu cầu vốn lưu động, triển khai dự án.
Tuy nhiên, cần nhìn nhận rằng lượng tiền tăng thêm không hoàn toàn đồng nghĩa với dòng tiền tự do được tạo ra từ hoạt động kinh doanh. Một phần đáng kể nguồn lực tài chính đến từ tiền khách hàng ứng trước để thực hiện các hợp đồng, dự án.
Cuối quý III, người mua trả tiền trước ngắn hạn đạt hơn 2.416 tỷ đồng, tăng khoảng 1.432 tỷ đồng so với đầu năm. Trong đó, các khoản ứng trước liên quan đến hai dự án điện sinh khối của Erex Tuyên Quang và Erex Yên Bái lần lượt ở mức hơn 914 tỷ đồng và 929 tỷ đồng. Ngoài ra, TV2 nhận ứng trước khoảng 467 tỷ đồng từ Ban quản lý dự án ngành điện thuộc Tập đoàn Công nghiệp - Năng lượng Quốc gia Việt Nam (PVN).
Nguồn tiền ứng trước giúp doanh nghiệp chủ động hơn về vốn để triển khai hợp đồng, đồng thời hạn chế nhu cầu vay ngân hàng. Tuy nhiên, đây cũng là khoản tiền gắn với nghĩa vụ thực hiện dự án, không thể xem toàn bộ là nguồn lực sẵn có để sử dụng tùy ý. Hiệu quả kinh doanh cuối cùng còn phụ thuộc vào tiến độ triển khai, kiểm soát chi phí và khả năng bàn giao, nghiệm thu công trình.
Ở chiều ngược lại, các khoản phải thu ngắn hạn gia tăng, phản ánh lượng vốn đang nằm tại khách hàng và các đối tác. Một khoản phải thu đáng chú ý là khoảng 657 tỷ đồng liên quan đến CTCP Đầu tư Năng lượng Tái tạo Cà Mau. Quy mô công nợ lớn đòi hỏi TV2 tiếp tục theo dõi khả năng thu hồi, thời hạn thanh toán và chất lượng các khoản phải thu nhằm tránh áp lực vốn lưu động.
Tổng nợ phải trả cuối quý III đạt khoảng 3.488 tỷ đồng, tăng mạnh so với mức 1.704 tỷ đồng đầu năm. Phần lớn mức tăng đến từ các khoản khách hàng ứng trước, trong khi tổng nợ vay ngắn hạn ở mức gần 153 tỷ đồng, tương đương khoảng 11% vốn chủ sở hữu. Xét riêng đòn bẩy vay ngân hàng, TV2 chưa cho thấy áp lực quá lớn.
Nhìn tổng thể, TV2 ghi nhận một số tín hiệu tích cực như lợi nhuận tăng mạnh, tiền và tiền gửi ngân hàng ở mức cao, trong khi nợ vay thấp so với vốn chủ sở hữu. Dù vậy, tính bền vững của kết quả phục hồi vẫn phụ thuộc vào khả năng duy trì nguồn thu tài chính, hiệu quả triển khai các dự án và tốc độ thu hồi công nợ. Đây cũng là những yếu tố cần tiếp tục theo dõi trong các kỳ báo cáo tiếp theo.
Với nhà đầu tư, phiên tăng trần ngày 28/10 là diễn biến đáng chú ý của cổ phiếu TV2 trong bối cảnh doanh nghiệp ghi nhận lợi nhuận quý III tăng mạnh. Tuy nhiên, một phiên tăng giá chưa đủ để xác lập xu hướng dài hạn. Diễn biến cổ phiếu trong thời gian tới cần được theo dõi cùng kết quả kinh doanh các quý tiếp theo, dòng tiền thực tế và những thông tin chính thức liên quan đến vụ án.

articles.title: Marvell Lumentum deal: chipmaker nears buying the $85bn laser maker
articles.text:
Chipmaker Marvell Technology is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, which makes the lasers that move data between AI chips. Marvell would likely pay in shares, and the companies could announce a deal as soon as next week, according to Bloomberg.
Ryan Gould, Michelle F. Davis and David Carnevali reported the talks for Bloomberg on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. Valida Pau separately reported for The Information that the companies have been in talks, citing one person. TNW has not independently verified the reports.
Lumentum is worth about $85bn and Marvell about $196bn, Bloomberg reported. Bloomberg could not learn the terms. A deal would be one of the largest ever in the technology industry, according to Bloomberg.
Not agreed yet
The Marvell Lumentum deal is not final. The companies have not reached an agreement, and the talks could still end without one, the people told Bloomberg. The timing could also change. Bloomberg said it could not reach Marvell or Lumentum for comment.
Lumentum shares rose in extended trading on Wednesday after the report, Britney Nguyen reported for MarketWatch. On Thursday, Marvell fell as much as 14% in New York and Lumentum rose as much as 7%, according to Bloomberg. The Nasdaq 100 also fell, after big tech results renewed doubts about AI spending.
Why lasers matter
Lumentum makes lasers and other optical parts that send large amounts of data at high speed. AI data centres link growing clusters of processors. More of that traffic now moves over optical links instead of copper wires.
Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston said this month that its optical parts are sold out through early 2029, Bloomberg reported. He said the company will not be able to meet about 70% of demand for some products next year. Lumentum plans to invest at least $350m in Japan to make more indium phosphide components. In September, IQE’s chief executive warned about the supply of that material.
Marvell already buys lasers from Lumentum. It makes custom AI and networking chips and works with Amazon Web Services and Microsoft on their own AI chips. In August, it agreed a chip deal with Google. Earlier this year it bought Celestial AI, which builds photonic technology for moving data between processors.
Nvidia took a $2bn stake in Lumentum earlier this year, in a deal that included work together on photonics, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia also holds about $99bn in shares of companies that buy its chips.
What analysts said
The deal “makes strategic sense given the highly complementary product portfolios,” RBC Capital Markets analysts wrote, according to Bloomberg.
The RBC analysts said the case is strongest if Marvell sells Lumentum’s pluggable module business. Raymond James analysts wrote that an all-share deal avoids interest costs, so it would dilute earnings less. Marvell shareholders would give up more ownership, though.

articles.title: Ikea’s colorful donut-shaped smart lamp is $20 off
articles.text:
With its playful design, versatility, and relatively affordable price, the Ikea Varmblixt quickly became one of my colleague Jennifer Pattison Tuohy’s new favorite smart light products when she tested it in April. Now, the donut-shaped lamp is on sale for $79.99 ($20 off) through November 11th at Ikea.
Ikea’s colorful donut-shaped smart lamp is $20 off
The Varmblixt can display hundreds of colors thanks to its Matter support, and can be put on your table or wall
Don’t let us tell you where you can or cannot put your Varmblixt. But it’s meant to sit on a table or be mounted on a wall (it can hang from a drilled-in screw, nothing fancy). At just 180 lumens, it isn’t particularly bright, so it’s better suited for use as a bedside lamp or for mood lighting than being tasked to illuminate a room. The newer model lets you cycle through 12 preset colors, including shades of pink, blue, green, and white, as opposed to just orange with the predecessor. The included wireless remote lets you switch between colors, adjust the brightness, and turn the lamp on or off without needing an app or a separate hub (there’s a power button on the lamp itself) . You can also use the remote to control other compatible Ikea lights.
For those who want to embed the Varmblixt into their smart home setup, the lamp supports Matter, allowing it to work with compatible smart home platforms including Apple Home, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa. In addition to letting you control the lights with your voice, this gives you access to hundreds more colors, lets you set lighting schedules and sleep or wake-up routines, and allows you to connect the lamp with motion sensors and other smart lights you may have. You can unlock those features with Ikea’s Dirigera hub, as well, which also offers a feature through its Home Smart app that gradually adjusts the shade of white throughout the day akin to natural daylight.

articles.title: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When people have career or job questions, they usually tap into their network to find experts who’ve faced a similar predicament and can offer answers. Increasingly, that job is falling to AI.
SuperMe is a network of AI profiles built from the knowledge of real-life experts. When you ask a question, the platform determines which experts are best suited to answer and creates a group chat with their AI profiles.
To scale that network on both sides, meaning more users asking questions and more experts supplying knowledge, the startup announced today that it is raising $20 million in funding led by Kirsten Green at Forerunner, with participation from Greylock Partners.
Casey Winters and Ludo Antonov founded the startup in 2024. Both have experience at large consumer companies. Winters held exec roles at Grubhub, Pinterest, and Eventbrite and has advised companies like Airbnb and Canva part-time. Antonov was head of engineering at multiple startups, including Pinterest, Lyft, and Whatnot.
The two got connected when Winters was advising Whatnot. ChatGPT was becoming popular around the same time, and they decided to build a network business using AI.
“There are these hidden networks in Silicon Valley of who the best people are for niche skills. Our idea was: Could we make that network of who the absolute best people are more transparent, and could we take all of the key insights that are locked inside their heads and make them more readily available?” Winters told TechCrunch over a call.
Users can go to the SuperMe website and type their question into the chatbot to start a group of experts. They can also return to a group they have formed or joined and ask follow-up questions.
You can ask a question like “Analyze my pitch deck. Which parts of the story are the weakest,
and which questions should I be most prepared to answer?” and get answers from AI profiles of longtime VCs like Mercedes Bent, Sarah Tavel, and Josh Elman. Users can also go to these people’s profiles and ask questions directly rather than in a group chat.
To collect knowledge from users, SuperMe scans public sources such as LinkedIn, YouTube, Substack, and blogs. It also draws on connected apps such as Google Drive, Notion, Gmail, and meeting notetaking tools like Granola. SuperMe said some of this data will include personal information and trade secrets, but it makes sure that none of it appears in answers.
The network is currently free, but the startup plans to cap the number of questions users can ask, after which they will have to cough up some money. It is also considering how to give experts incentives to add more knowledge.
SuperMe also works with MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard that lets AI chatbots connect to outside tools and data), so users can ask questions from within chatbots such as Claude and ChatGPT.
The startup has about 13 employees. It is hiring on the tech side to improve its AI models for conversation and for matching questions to experts, and on the network side for someone to find experts in subject areas the platform doesn’t yet cover.
Forerunner’s Green said that SuperMe is well positioned to build a platform where AI collaborates with humans.
“I think it’s one of the reasons why this is very timely, and it’s good to have something like this establishing itself when we’re relatively early in this journey,” she told TechCrunch over a call. “Because there’s going to be so many lessons that are going to be learned, and they need to be shared so that people can come along in a productive way. I think that the balance here is to build a network so that you do have a true sharing component where there are incentives and benefits for everybody to contribute what they know.”

articles.title: FuriosaAI Series D: $620m quadruples the chipmaker’s value to $2.9bn
articles.text:
FuriosaAI, a Seoul-based maker of AI inference chips, has raised $620m in a Series D round. The round values it at about $2.9bn. South Korea’s National Growth Fund put in $280m, making it the largest investor.
The company announced the round in a press release and a blog post. Its previous round last year valued it at $735m, so its valuation has quadrupled, Yoolim Lee reported for Bloomberg, which had the news first.
“We see strong demand and opportunities as we are scaling our business globally,” chief executive June Paik said on Bloomberg Television on Thursday.
Who invested
International investors put $110m into the FuriosaAI Series D. US firm Infinitum was the largest of them. Jericho Capital, Worldline Capital, Cisco Investments, Abu Dhabi’s NeoFort Holding and Singapore’s QUDA Capital Partners joined it. QUDA’s founder, Charlie Foo, is a former Nvidia executive and now advises FuriosaAI.
Existing shareholders added $125m, including all three seed investors: NAVER, DSC Investment and KDB Capital. The Export-Import Bank of Korea made its first direct investment in a startup, and asset manager UAMCO committed $30m.
“Taking an advanced AI chip from design to volume production is an exceptionally difficult undertaking, and few companies have demonstrated the ability to do so successfully,” said John Yetimoglu, chief investment officer at Infinitum.
The chip and its customers
Nvidia chips dominate AI data centres, and investors are looking for alternatives that use less energy, Bloomberg reported. FuriosaAI builds chips for inference, the work of running trained AI models, rather than training them.
Its second-generation chip, RNGD, pronounced “renegade”, went into mass production in January. TSMC is making 20,000 of them this year, according to Bloomberg. FuriosaAI says it has secured the memory and factory capacity to make more than 40,000 in 2027. Memory is scarce across the industry: Micron expects the memory shortage to tighten into 2028.
The RNGD card draws 180 watts and needs only air cooling. FuriosaAI says it matches the throughput of Nvidia’s RTX PRO 6000 card for card. It also says RNGD serves twice as many users per kilowatt. TNW has not tested these claims.
Samsung SDS launched a cloud service running on RNGD in July. LG Group runs its EXAONE models on the chips, according to FuriosaAI. Korean AI company Upstage uses them for search summaries. Paik told Bloomberg the company is talking to many customers in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
What the money is for
FuriosaAI will use the money to make more RNGD chips, improve its software and build its third-generation chip. FuriosaAI is developing that chip with Broadcom and other partners. It will use a 2nm, multi-die design with HBM4 memory, the company says.
The company has offices in the United States, Singapore and Lisbon. In Lisbon, it brought RNGD to Europe with Equinix in July. Other inference chipmakers have also raised large rounds this year, including Etched at $21bn in August.

articles.title: Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros
articles.text:
The new MacBook Pro brings with it a bunch of firsts for Apple laptops, the two flashiest being an OLED display and touchscreen functionality. But as an image-accuracy enthusiast, trained calibrator, and resident display expert, what excites me most about the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the technology it uses to display an accurate picture. It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes. It could be the future for displays.
Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros
CMFs, or color-matching functions, mathematically represent how we perceive color, and there are a few different variations. The specification that’s been the standard for years is CIE 1931 (CIE stands for Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage, or International Commission on Illumination). For nearly a century, CIE 1931 has been a reliable calibration target, and most of the reference modes on the new MacBook use it.
But with the development of new display technologies over the past 20 years that have ultra-narrow band spectra — such as OLED, LEDs with KSF phosphors, and quantum dots — CIE 1931’s shortcomings are increasingly apparent. Even when calibrated to the same D65 white point, the same image on an OLED and quantum dot LED can look identical to one person, but different to another because of biological variations in our eyes. We all have small discrepancies in our eyes — such as the sensitivity of the cones in our eyes, which allow us to see color — and those can change as we age. CIE 1931 doesn’t properly handle that and was created based on only 17 test subjects. It’s not ideal in a professional setting where content needs to look the same regardless of the screen technology it’s on or who’s viewing it. Apple CMF 2026 addresses that, so that displays look the same regardless of the technology they use.
Apple first included its new CMF on the Studio Display XDR, which I reviewed earlier this year and found to be an excellent, albeit expensive, monitor for color professionals because of Apple CMF 2026 and the reference color modes. But the fact that this technology is now on a laptop that’s portable and not just a standalone monitor living on a desk is a big help for professionals on the move.
As on the Studio Display XDR, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has two Apple CMF 2026 reference modes — one for P3 color primaries and one that includes both P3 and Adobe RGB color primaries for more flexibility. Peak brightness with both HDR and SDR content is 2,000 nits (on the XDR monitor peak SDR luminance is up to 1,000 nits), and the True Tone setting automatically adjusts HDR tone mapping, brightness, and white point based on ambient lighting. (An option to disable True Tone is in Displays preferences.)
The MacBook doesn’t require using Apple CMF 2026, as there are 14 more reference color modes that use the CIE 1931 color space — it is still the standard, after all — including DICOM for medical imaging (which is cool, but only useful to those in the medical field). The MacBook also supports Apple Pro Display Calibrator, which includes three calibration methods to adjust the reference color modes, or a custom mode, if necessary. There are options for a full calibration or to fine-tune a calibration with the proper measurement gear, or to visually fine-tune the display.
Color science and display technologies have come a long way since 1931, when the CIE 1931 color space was established. Apple’s development of the Apple CMF 2026 and its standardization efforts — the company is currently working with a CIE technical committee on a proposed standard — is an important step to make sure current display technologies look the same to as many people as possible.
Extending support to the new MacBook expands the user base considerably (let’s face it, more people are buying a touchscreen MacBook, even at $2,900, than a $3,300 professional monitor). And more importantly, it gives professionals that can get the most out of it easier, portable access.

articles.title: Agent identity startup Mintive lands Cowboy Ventures, Coatue, angels Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Here’s another early-stage, agent-management startup to watch because of the backgrounds of the founders and the sheer number of big names it has already attracted as investors: Mintive.
Mintive has raised $11 million total, including a newly announced $7 million seed led by Cowboy Ventures. Additional investors include Coatue, Operator Collective, and Hustle Fund; angels include Okta co-founder Frederic Kerrest, Discovery Loop co-founder and former Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean, and OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy, among others.
Mintive was founded by Jiquan Ngiam (pictured above, far right) and Vijay Vasudevan (pictured above far left). Ngiam, Mintive’s CEO, was the founding engineer of Coursera (employee No. 1, hired by Andrew Ng). Ngiam later worked on neural networks at Google Brain. Vasudevan, the company’s CTO, is best known as one of the co-creators of TensorFlow while he was at Google Brain. That was the OG AI training platform that predated PyTorch.
Mintive is joining a crowded field of products that promise to govern, provision, and offer identity management to enterprise AI agents. Its platform includes an MCP gateway that allows IT professionals to authorize what the cloud services agents may access and what actions they can perform on them. It also offers an LLM gateway that routes to different models and can cap costs; handles agent identities and authorizations that may differ from the employees that they serve; and an agent monitor that tracks all agents across the company. The company also allows enterprises to create agents that proactively perform long-running tasks.
Still, it’s hard to imagine a field with more competition. Agent management systems are offered by Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, plus as point products galore (from companies as diverse as LangChain, New Relic, and Rippling, to name a few). Then there are countless startups working on the idea (40+ from Y Combinator alone).
So, what’s Mintive’s secret sauce? Given the founders’ long history in building AI for enterprises, they have designed their system to be especially easy to use, Ngiam says. Set-up amounts to clicking a few buttons, the startup promises.
“I think what our customers look at and they are a bit shocked at, is how quick it is and easy to deploy,” Ngiam tells TechCrunch. “We have really thought through all the ways this can be done, all the access control, permissioning layer, to make it so easy for them to deploy it, that all the complexities are hidden away. You don’t think about sandboxes, you don’t think about harnesses, you don’t think about memory because we manage that for you.”
That pitch has won over 50 enterprise customers so far, Mintive says, since the startup launched its product in February. These include Ro, Modern Treasury, the University of Michigan, Coursera, Apax, and Stability AI.
But it was the founders’ industry experience that won over Cowboy Ventures managing partner Aileen Lee.
“AI is going to be able to power incredible things, but we need more infrastructure that’s going to give us governance and visibility and control,” Lee told TechCrunch.
Lee also says she particularly respects that Ngiam has been careful by only raising $11 million. This compares to other agentic-building startups raising vast amounts at unicorn valuations. As just one example: Prime Intellect raised $130 million for its Series A at $1 billion valuation.
“I feel really lucky to have won the chance to work with him,” said Lee. “He is a grown-up and so he was not a person chasing a ‘vanity’ round.”
Lee added: “I think a lot of companies are being set up for failure by chasing round size, rather than, ‘how much do I need to actually really move the needle for the company?’ And so, yes, in a time when people are raising unprecedented amounts of money, we’re just kind of doing it the brick by brick, old-fashioned way.”

articles.title: Intel plunges on a major guidance miss. What went wrong — and how to proceed
articles.text: Intel delivered a solid quarter on Thursday, but its guidance underscored how heavily it still depends on the struggling PC market, sending shares sharply lower after hours. We're not joining the sell-off just yet. Revenue in the third quarter increased 21% year over year to $16.513 billion, edging out the LSEG-compiled consensus estimate of $16.496 billion. Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) more than doubled to 52 cents, beating the LSEG estimate of 40 cents. INTC YTD mountain Intel 1-year return Bottom line Despite data center demand and improvements at its foundry still pointing to a solid long-term outlook, analysts will need to revise estimates downward for several quarters, as weakness in the consumer electronics market will persist well into 2027. Why not bail on the stock? This is the reset. Further downside is certainly possible, but selling now won't erase the losses we've taken. Looking ahead to next year, we see the data center business continuing to grow as agentic AI workloads drive demand for CPUs, foundry operations continue to improve, and the PC market bottoms out. As a result, the risk/reward profile dictates we stick with it, even if the outlook suggests this probably isn't the best use case for new money into year-end. We'll be more optimistic once the downward estimate revisions come through, the stock finds its bottom, and most importantly, when we see evidence that the inventory flush currently underway in the PC market is coming to an end. There is no doubt that upside is capped for the near future. As a result, our rating is currently under review, and we are slashing our price target to $100. Commentary Memory prices are through the roof. Data center builders are all too happy to pay up and can raise capital by issuing debt or selling equity. Consumers can't, putting immense pressure on the PC market. Consumer demand isn't driving the surge in memory prices. The issue is that PC makers and the data center cohort rely on the same manufacturing capacity, and there simply isn't enough of it to meet demand from both. For example, Apple has raised prices on some Macs and iPads to offset higher memory costs. Its devices don't use the same high-bandwidth memory sought by the likes of Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms, but Apple is competing with those data center players for the limited capacity at memory supplier fabs (think Samsung, Micron, and SK Hynix). "The industry continues to navigate one of the most significant supply shortages in history driven by the unprecedented demand for superintelligence," CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on the conference call. While Intel has done a lot to expand its data center business — and benefited immensely from the need for its CPUs to power agentic AI workloads — it remains heavily exposed to the PC market. Sales in the unit fell 5% year-over-year, but it still accounts for more than half of the revenue of Intel's products group (CCPG + DCAI) and about 43% of Intel Products' operating income (see chart below). That PC exposure is weighing on Intel's outlook for the rest of the year, even as it reported its strongest DCAI (data center and AI) segment growth in 15 years. "In recent weeks, our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on the memory prices and availability," Tan said. Still, the quarterly results were largely better than expected. Sales outpaced expectations, driven by strength in the Data Center AI and Foundry segments, partially offset by a miss in the Client Computing and Physical AI Group, which has exposure to the PC market. Adjusted gross margin expansion met expectations, contributing to a strong adjusted operating income result and setting the stage for the earnings beat. Cash flow was also strong, with Intel reporting an inflow, whereas the Street expected an outflow. CEO Tan said demand for 2027 is "significant, especially in CPU-dense rack-scale infrastructure." However, if Intel is going to capitalize on the opportunity, it needs to ramp up its manufacturing capacity. According to Tan, there are three key hurdles to overcome: improve efficiency (yields and cycle times); solve the industry-wide shortage of advanced organic substrates needed for packaging, which is also hindering output ramp-up; and recover from an extended shutdown at one of the company's factories in Israel, which will impact server CPU shipments in the current quarter and possibly beyond. On the call, CFO David Zinsner estimated a $300 million impact in the fourth quarter, which is "likely to be similar in the first quarter." Why we own it Intel is benefiting from the AI boom in multiple ways: Its data center CPUs are in demand to support AI agent-driven tasks, while its foundry business allows it to manufacture its own processors as well as chips designed by other companies. Competitors : Taiwan Semiconductor , AMD , Arm Holdings Most recent buy : Aug. 10, 2026 Initiated : June 3, 2026 "Purpose-built silicon remains our fastest-growing business segment, tripling over the last three years and poised to triple again over the next few years," Tan added. "We see further growth opportunity with both existing and new potential customers, including AI labs, and expanding our IP portfolio to meet the needs of a wider array of customers." Intel estimates that agentic AI workloads could expand the total addressable market for server CPUs fivefold over the next five years, from $40 billion today to as much as $200 billion. Intel's foundry business continued to show improvement, with revenue increasing 16% sequentially. Most of the output is for Intel's own use, so it doesn't count toward reported revenue. External revenue rose $118 million from the prior quarter to $411 million, though the increase was primarily due to a non-recurring customer program. Analysts, including us, tend to discount non-recurring revenue when assessing a business's health. The unit remains unprofitable, but its operating margin was roughly half as bad as a year ago. articles.title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
articles.text:
Microsoft on Thursday announced plans to raise $25 billion in bonds, taking advantage of its healthy credit rating to support its infrastructure expansion.
The software maker holds a top-tier AAA rating with S&P, a credit agency. Management is targeting $170 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, as the company looks to meet heavy demand from artificial intelligence labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients.
"Microsoft intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, funding for working capital, capital expenditures, repurchases of capital stock, acquisitions, and repayment of existing debt," according to a statement. The offerings should close on Nov. 4, the company said.
Amazon and Alphabet have engaged the bond market to support infrastructure projects this year, and AI-focused cloud CoreWeave has also relied on the debt market to broaden its data center footprint. Investors have turned more skittish on companies with tall debt piles as central bankers raise interest rates to fight inflation.
Microsoft will access additional funding sources to complement its own cash flow generation when conditions are attractive, Amy Hood, its finance chief, said on the company's earnings call on Wednesday.
"There's a form of financing called leasing, and we've been using that one as a vehicle," she said. "We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our ratings are, and we haven't yet tapped that."
Microsoft reported positive free cash flow on Wednesday, differentiating itself from Alphabet, whose cash flow was negative for the second quarter in a row. Last week Meta said it had negative free cash flow, and on Thursday Amazon reported negative free cash flow.
Also on Wednesday, Oracle unveiled plans to raise $10 billion in new debt and said it anticipates a return to positive free cash flow in the second half of its 2028 fiscal year.

articles.title: Bitcoin tumbles below $78,000, extending losses as Binance security scare rattles crypto markets
articles.text:
Bitcoin fell below $78,000 on Friday as concerns over a potential security breach at cryptocurrency exchange Binance rattled digital asset markets, prompting several major crypto firms to freeze billions of dollars in funds linked to the incident.
The world's largest cryptocurrency fell over 4% to $77,994.96, extending its losses after breaking below the psychologically important $80,000 threshold.
Ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4.84% to $2,247.45, while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 7.68% to $694.45.
Defying the broader sell-off, Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged 9.7% to $89.08.
Several cryptocurrency firms, including stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether, froze a combined $2.54 billion in funds linked to the suspected incident on Thursday.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USD Coin, while Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the firm had halted transactions involving more than $1.5 billion in USDT potentially connected to the breach.
Ripple also helped prevent the movement of $200 million in funds linked to the suspected attack, according to Binance co-founder Yi He.
Blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identified nearly $6 billion in digital assets across 55 wallet addresses potentially associated with the incident, suggesting the scale of the suspected breach could be significantly larger than the amount frozen.
Binance has not explicitly confirmed that a hack occurred, saying it was investigating reports of a potential security issue.
"Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said, adding that user funds remained safe.
Binance founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao also sought to reassure investors that customer funds were secure, although he said the incident appeared to be a hack.
The developments have renewed concerns over security vulnerabilities in the cryptocurrency industry, which has suffered a string of major breaches in recent years.
In 2025, cryptocurrency exchange Bybit suffered a roughly $1.5 billion hack, while rival Bitget more recently lost over $350 million in digital assets to cyber theft.
—CNBC's Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report.

articles.title: FedEx Freight delivers a much-needed quarterly beat. Where we stand on shares now
articles.text: FedEx Freight on Thursday night took a positive step forward in its young journey as a standalone public company. In its first official earnings report since being spun off in June, the less-than-truckload shipping provider delivered a top and bottom line beat and offered encouraging commentary on its self-help improvements. Revenue in the three months ended in September rose 8% to $2.44 billion, beating the LSEG consensus of $2.33 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) totaled $1.49, exceeding the consensus of $1.36, LSEG data showed. Bottom line Shares rose about 3% in extended trading, a welcome market reaction considering how badly the stock has struggled. After a decent debut in June, FedEx Freight has been drifting lower, seemingly with no end. Anytime a stock is spun off, there can be an adjustment period as investors who received shares due to ownership in its former parent decide to dump it. Plus, elevated fuel prices have weighed on stocks across the transportation industry, complicating matters for FDXF shares. As a reminder, FedEx Freight is a less-than-truckload carrier. LTL services consolidate shipments from multiple customers onto a single trailer. Think of these shipments as too large for standard parcel delivery, such as something over 150 pounds or a few pallets of product, but not big enough for the customer to need a whole truck. Its competitors include Old Dominion Freight Line , XPO and J.B. Hunt . FDXF ALL mountain FedEx Freight's stock performance since its June debut. Though it hasn't been fun to endure this drawdown in FDXF, we haven't bailed on the name because our investment thesis centers on FedEx Freight making operational improvements now that it's no longer part of FedEx Corp . We recognized that it cannot be accomplished overnight. That's what made Thursday's earnings report such an anticipated event — a chance to update investors on its progress and show what's in store for next year. Aside from an August investor conference, we haven't heard from Freight management since late June, when the company discussed the results of its final quarter inside FedEx. For example, Freight believes it has more leverage in pricing negotiations as a standalone company than it did under FedEx, where contracts were bundled with package delivery and other transportation services. "Since June 1, we have successfully renewed approximately 25% of our contractual portfolio and achieved our strongest renewal pricing performance in recent years," FedEx Freight CEO John Smith said Thursday night. "Given that approximately two-thirds of our revenue is generated under negotiated customer pricing agreements, we believe our contractual renewal performance provides meaningful support for future yield improvement." Another benefit of being on its own: FedEx Freight has built up a dedicated salesforce focused on the less-than-truckload market, where the company is pursuing winning more business in attractive industries. "When you think about some of the verticals where we see some improvement, one of them is in aerospace. We landed a few new accounts, as well as grown some of the existing accounts. And we're up, through the first four months, about 3%," Smith said. "That's one example. We're seeing movement in food. We're seeing movement in some of technology. Probably the one that we've seen the most success in is the retail space, and we continue to grow that. We feel pretty good about our plan, and how we're going after and attacking these verticals. So, more to come, and I think you'll see more progress as we move forward on our next quarter and into 2027. We still prefer FedEx Corp over FedEx Freight at this juncture, and our position weightings in the portfolio reflect this sentiment. But Freight's stock has come down hard despite generally solid results, so we'll continue holding this spin-off for now. We're reiterating our buy-equivalent 1 rating. However, we are reducing our price target to $160 from $175 to better reflect the price-to-earnings multiple compression the trucking group has experienced over the past four months due to the restart of the Middle East conflict and associated rise in fuel prices. For its part, FedEx reported better-than-exected results of its own Wednesday night. Though shares were down a few percentage points in Wednesday's extended trading, likely due to a soft current-quarter outlook, the stock encouragingly finished up 1% in Thursday's regular session. That suggests investors agreed with us and were unfazed by the guide. Commentary In addition to the strong headline results, FedEx Freight reported a 1.1% year-over-year increase in revenue per shipment (ex-fuel surcharges) to $316.78, helping to more than offset a 0.7% decline in average daily shipments. Also notable, the cadence of average daily shipments has been improving each month since March. For the reported period, shipments were down 3.4% in June, improving to minus 2.2% in July, minus 0.7% in August, and flipping to up 0.9% in September. Another positive: 98% on-time service and pick-up reliability should also help the company steal some share from others in the LTL space, during the crucial shopping season. The company's claims ratio and the frequency of claims have both continued to trend lower since 2022, exiting the period at 0.43% and 0.27%, respectively. This is a sign of improved customer service quality, which is good to see no matter what industry you're talking about. Guidance Fourth-quarter guidance is as follows: Revenue of $2.30 billion to $2.37 billion, ahead of the $2.2 billion expected, according to LSEG. Adjusted operating income between $185 and $205 million, ahead of the $172 million FactSet consensus estimate. articles.title: How elections worldwide are testing Trump’s influence abroad
articles.text:
In August, President Donald Trump claimed that 97% of Republican candidates he backed had won their primary races.
And it's true that Trump has shown an ability to influence races particularly in Republican primaries, picking off politicians he didn't like such as Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky.
But while he hasn't shied away from expressing his opinions on foreign leaders, his influence over other countries' elections is proving less strong.
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection on Sunday, defeating Trump-aligned Flávio Bolsonaro, whose father Jair had also been a Trump ally.
Also last weekend, a student-led movement in Serbia defeated the ruling party of Aleksandar Vucic, a populist leader who had cultivated ties with Trump and his circle. Vucic had served as Serbia's president from 2017, and as prime minister from 2014 to 2017.
During his concession speech, Vucic said that the loss was due to a "legitimization of a revolution carried out by the people with direct support from various European countries and the American deep state, the one that opposes President Trump."
Earlier this year, Vice President JD Vance had visited Hungary for two days and publicly backed then-Prime Minister Viktor Orban. However, Orban, who is also a staunch ally and endorsed by Trump, lost that election and was ejected from office after 16 years.
In October, Trump also endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection. While the results of the Oct. 27 election are not finalized yet, the Associated Press said that Netanhayu's Likud party had appeared to lose its majority in the country's parliament.
Still, Trump's influence on any one global election remains variable, experts said.
"Elections are always national first and regional or global a very distant second," Cas Mudde, professor of international affairs at the University of Georgia, told CNBC.
Furthermore, it is also not clear that Trump ever had a great influence over far-right actors elsewhere, said Stijn van Kessel, professor of comparative politics at Queen Mary University of London.
"Far-right parties and politicians like to celebrate each others' victories as it allows them to portray themselves as part of a successful global movement," he said, adding that those relationships can sour quickly when national interests collide and the foreign partner turns toxic in the eyes of the domestic electorate.
Van Kessel pointed to the fallout between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni earlier this year, which stemmed from Italy's refusal to allow U.S. aircraft to use one of the NATO airbases for its war on Iran.
Trump later claimed that Meloni "begged" him for a photo at the G7 summit, a claim that sparked a denial from Meloni.
Right wing strength
Still, right-wing movements remain strong in numerous places globally. In France, Marine Le Pen is currently the frontrunner to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, according to a compilation of polls by Politico. However, historically she has often started out leading a crowded field of hopefuls before support consolidates around a more moderate candidate.
In Germany, the far-right Alternative fur Deutschland, or AfD party won 20.8% of the vote in the country's February 2025 federal election, making it the country's largest opposition party. Trump ally Javier Milei leads Argentina, and Colombia's new President Abelardo de la Espriella was elected on a far-right platform.
Still, Mudde noted that most far-right leaders disassociate themselves from Trump when he becomes more unpopular in their country. Trump's poll numbers remain near a record low even in the U.S. over issues including the Iran war and the cost of living as energy prices soar.
"Voters are willing to give anyone a shot when they are economically frustrated, but when those experiments fail, they move on to something else," said David Barker, a professor of government at American University in Washington, D.C. At this point, Trump "undermines his allies' ability to maintain support."

articles.title: Starbucks serves up a solid quarter and full-year outlook. Why we're staying invested
articles.text: Starbucks on Thursday reported better-than-expected quarterly profits to wrap up its fiscal 2026 and issued healthy guidance for its new year. The results and outlook may not convince any skeptics to change their tune, especially as elevated gas prices remain a threat to consumer spending. However, we see plenty of encouraging reasons to stay invested and bet on CEO Brian Niccol. Revenue in its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter was $9.14 billion, slightly missing the LSEG consensus of $9.23 billion. Quarterly revenue declined 4.5% year over year, primarily due to its China business moving to a joint-venture model from company-operated stores. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) in the July-to-September period increased 54% on an annual basis to 80 cents, topping the 72-cent consensus, LSEG data showed. Global comparable store sales, a key performance metric in the restaurant industry, were up 7.2% in the quarter. That exceeded the FactSet consensus of 6%. North America comparable store sales increased 7.9% in the quarter, beating expectations of 7% growth. SBUX YTD mountain Starbucks YTD Shares of Starbucks were down about 2% in extended trading Thursday. That could reflect some profit-taking following a strong comeback for the stock in recent weeks. Like many restaurant stocks, Starbucks suffered a bruising decline beginning in late August and into October, driven primarily by concerns that resurgent gas prices in the U.S. may put a crimp on consumer spending. The stock lost more than 16% between Aug. 26 and Oct. 9. However, it has since erased most of those losses and, as of Thursday's close, sat less than 3% from its highest close of the year on Aug. 11. We're reiterating our hold-equivalent 2 rating and keeping our price target of $120 a share. Bottom line Starbucks is on solid ground as Niccol enters his third full fiscal year leading the coffee chain. Investors are no longer satisfied with reinvigorated top-line growth. They want to see continued sales momentum translate into stronger profits. We think Niccol is doing just that, reflected in Starbucks' fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EPS exceeding consensus and its initial fiscal 2027 guidance at least meeting expectations on adjusted operating margin and profits. Bears may still be concerned about valuation, with shares trading at 33 times forward earnings. That's a tough debate to settle at the moment. For the stock to work, Starbucks will need to execute and deliver upside in the coming quarters — making the stock look cheaper in the rearview mirror than it appeared. With Niccol steering the ship, that's a bet we're willing to make. And it's no longer about his track record at Chipotle . At Starbucks, he's delivered three earnings beats in a row, following an uneven start to his tenure, which began in the fall of 2024. All the changes that Niccol had to make — adding staffing to cafes, streamlining the menu, closing underperforming locations and starting renovations of surviving locations to make them more inviting places to be — are bearing fruit. "Back to Starbucks, as a strategy, has switched gears from a turnaround plan to a growth plan," Niccol said on Thursday's earnings call. The company has delivered five straight quarters of positive global comparable store sales growth, or comps. In North America, comps exceeded Wall Street expectations for the sixth earnings report in a row. Looking ahead, Starbucks said it expects North America comps to grow 4% in fiscal 2027 — slightly below the 4.2% consensus on FactSet. For comparison, full-year comps in fiscal 2026 rose 6.6%. Some deceleration is very much expected. And considering Niccol has a long-term target of at least 3% comps growth, it's notable that the fiscal 2027 guide came in above that. Asked about the comps outlook, Niccol said, "We just see strength in the business that gave us the confidence to commit to 4% comps." He added, "The way I look at it is, we're probably a year ahead of schedule relative to the guidance that we gave for fiscal '28" at our January investor day . The CEO pointed to the way that improved customer service has resonated, along with a redesigned digital rewards program that has grown to 36 million active users over the past 90 days, up from 35.8 million in July. Starbucks is working to add more personalization to the rewards program to fuel its next leg, Niccol said. Niccol also said the strength of the business stems from compelling marketing behind menu innovations such as protein cold foam, its iced Refreshers, and food upgrades. He mentioned there's more to come on the food front, particularly to drive transactions in the afternoon, and teased new tea drinks that lean into health and wellness. "The business is on really strong footing, and it is driven by operational health," Niccol said. He added, "Starbucks brand affinity is at near record levels as our menu innovation, marketing and merchandise continue to create moments that drive culture and bring people into our coffee houses." The marketing engine is revving up in the coming months with special holiday cups — most notably the return of last year's viral sensation: the Bearista glass cold cup. A few more thoughts on fiscal 2027: Starbucks is planning to increase the number of cafe uplifts to about 2,000 in North America, up from more than 1,700 in fiscal 2026. Niccol also said it will be year of major tech modernization, including new point-of-sale and staffing systems. Guidance Here is the full look at Starbucks' initial guidance for fiscal 2027 (which includes 53 weeks instead of its usual 52 weeks): Consolidated net revenue down 1%, including a $700 million from the extra week. The decline is primarily driven by the fact China was still company-operated for the first half of fiscal 2026. North America comparable store sales growth of roughly 4%, a touch below the 4.2% consensus on FactSet. Adjusted operating margin in the range of 13.5% to 14%, which even on the low end exceeds the 13.3% expectation. Adjusted EPS in the range of $3.15 to $3.25, including slightly more than 10 cents from the 53rd week. The midpoint of $3.20 edged out the FactSet consensus of $3.16 and represents almost 18% year-over-year growth. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long SBUX. See here for a full list of the stocks.) articles.title: We're cutting our Amazon price target after a rough quarter. But it isn't all bad
articles.text: Amazon on Thursday evening delivered a rare double miss. Shares of the e-commerce and cloud giant sank in after-hours trading as quarterly revenue and earnings fell short of estimates. Weaker-than-expected retail sales and advertising revenue offset strong Amazon Web Services numbers. Current quarter guidance also missed, though management was probably being conservative there. Revenue increased 12% year over year to $201.9 billion, missing the consensus analyst estimate of $202.3 billion, according to LSEG data. Earnings per share based on generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) fell 3% year over year to $1.89, missing the consensus estimate of $1.96, according to LSEG. Operating Income of $28 billion beat analyst forecasts by about $1.8 billion, according to FactSet. AMZN YTD mountain Amazon YTD Amazon's roughly 6.5% post-earnings slide followed up a 4% decline during the regular session. Bottom line At around $228 per share, the Club stock has given back the entire 15% pop it got last quarter , when CEO Andy Jassy explained the line of sight he has on achieving attractive returns on the company's data center investments. While Jassy's vision remains clear, the market has become much more skeptical about the returns on each dollar invested in AI infrastructure and how companies will fund these massive spending programs, especially as free cash flow turned negative, as it has for Amazon. Add in the slowdown in Amazon's core retail businesses — online stores and advertising — and it was a recipe for a disappointing quarter. Still, we see plenty to like about Amazon, including its multiyear AWS growth outlook that could move forward estimates higher, improving margins that allow management to keep reinvesting in the business and make its products and services strong, and likely conservative guidance that will be beat. But a miss is a miss. The long-term drivers keep us positive on the stock as we're reiterating our buy-equivalent 1 rating. We are, however, trimming our price target to $280 from $300 in recognition of the shifting investor expectations and the stock's drop from its record closing high of $284 back on Aug. 3. Commentary Revenue growth at cloud unit Amazon Web Services (AWS) accelerated for the sixth straight quarter. At 39.3% year over year, AWS recorded its fastest growth rate in nearly five years. This result was better than what analysts forecasted, but investor expectations may have been for a bigger quarter-over-quarter increase, especially after the strong cloud results from Microsoft and Alphabet on Wednesday night. AWS revenue was $45.98 billion, up from $42.23 billion in the second quarter. One important driver of AWS' growth was Bedrock, which the company said has become the fastest-growing multibillion-dollar service in the cloud unit's history. Amazon Bedrock is an AWS service that allows businesses to build and deploy generative AI applications using foundation models from leading AI companies without having to manage the underlying infrastructure. AWS operating income and operating margin also beat expectations. The fast sales growth led to strong operating leverage, with margins bumping up to 38.65% from 33.64% a year ago. In total, AWS operating income of $17.77 billion beat the consensus estimate of $16.97 billion. Once again, we heard Jassy tout the performance of its portfolio of in-house chips, such as Graviton and Trainium. After previously telling the Street there was a "real chance" Amazon would begin selling its chips directly to customers outside AWS, Jassy said the company now plans to start doing so in late 2027. The AWS backlog closed the quarter at $578 billion, up triple digits year over year and 16% from the second quarter. The backlog gives Jassy the confidence to project AWS revenue will grow by over 40% in both 2027 and 2028. That's well above the current consensus estimate of 35.47% in 2027 and 34.8% in 2028. In the next five to 10 years, Jassy believes AWS can be a $1 trillion revenue business. As for the rest of Amazon's business segments, there were solid revenue beats across Third-Party Seller Services, Subscription Services, and Other (which includes healthcare, licensing, co-branded credit cards, and other businesses). However, Online Stores, Physical Stores , and Advertising missed. These misses are outweighing the positives because Online Stores are the foundation of Amazon's retail business and Advertising is a high-margin revenue stream. Amazon's soft advertising numbers follow the miss we saw from Alphabet. Amazon attributed its slowdown in advertising growth to "timing anomalies," including the shift of Prime Day into the second quarter in most countries, the timing of NBA games on Prime Video, and changes to its search engine marketing programs in the third quarter of last year that drove more traffic to Amazon's search pages. Amazon expects advertising revenue growth to return to the high teens in the fourth quarter. An important part of the call came when Andy Jassy discussed the potential impact of agentic shopping on Amazon's advertising business, or rather, why he expects little to no impact at all. The concern when Meta Platforms launched Muse was that personal AI agents would buy products on Amazon on behalf of users, bypassing sponsored listings and potentially undermining Amazon's advertising business. While that may still be a possibility in the future, agentic shopping has yet to gain enough traction to meaningfully impact Amazon's advertising business. "Few customers are doing much shopping this way yet, as the experience is still not great nor more convenient than coming to a retailer directly to research or one-click order there," Jassy said on the call. By region, North America sales increased 6% year over year to $112.8 billion, missing the consensus estimate by about $370 million. Operating margins expanded 322 basis points over last year to 7.73%. In the International segment, revenue increased 5% year over year, but that missed by about $450 million.Operating margins expanded by 73 basis points. On the Capital Expenditures side, Amazon spent approximately $77 billion in the quarter, up from $53 billion in the second quarter and $44 billion in the first quarter. The company reiterated its expectation of $220 billion in capex this year, so a significant step down is expected in the fourth quarter. But Amazon still expects to spend "meaningfully more" next year "with a clear line of sight to attractive financial returns." Free cash flow over the past 12 months is negative $42.4 billion. Guidance Amazon provided guidance for the current fourth quarter that was slightly below the street. These forecasts are usually pretty conservative, but the market is placing a lot of emphasis on it because it's the holiday quarter for online stores. For the fourth quarter, Amazon guided net sales to the range of $240 billion and $247 billion. This midpoint of $243.5 billion is below the Street consensus estimate of $244.16 billion. Fourth quarter operating income is expected to be between $28.5 billion and $33.5 billion. This midpoint of $31 billion is below the Street consensus estimate of $33 billion. articles.title: Jim Cramer says Wall Street is punishing the wrong tech stocks
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Thursday that disappointing results from one company don't necessarily signal trouble for an entire industry.
Stocks fell Thursday, snapping a three-day winning streak as investors digested a fresh wave of corporate earnings. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 each slipped 0.4%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.4%. Cramer argued that investors are too quick to sell stocks alongside peers that are disappointing, overlooking key differences between businesses and creating potential buying opportunities.
"My motto: do the homework, know what the companies really do," the "Mad Money" host said. "That's the only way to profit from these short-term guilt-by-association moves, which tend to work themselves out."
He pointed to cybersecurity as a prime example. Fortinet's underwhelming quarterly results Wednesday dragged down shares of Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike, even though, Cramer argued, both competitors offer more comprehensive cybersecurity platforms. Unlike Fortinet, which is hardware-focused, Palo Alto and CrowdStrike provide broader suites of security products and services. Cramer said Fortinet has been losing market share to both companies, suggesting its weakness reflects company-specific challenges rather than a slowdown in industrywide demand.
"Their stocks should be bought, not sold, because Fortinet's weakness is not a tell about a slowdown in cybersecurity; it's just a sign that Fortinet itself isn't doing well," Cramer said.
He sees a similar disconnect in enterprise software, where ServiceNow's slight earnings disappointment Wednesday weighed on other software-as-a-service stocks, including Workday and Salesforce. Workday specializes in human resources and financial software, while Salesforce offers customer relationship management tools and its Agentforce platform.
"I am close to both Workday and Salesforce, and I can tell you that their declines today had more to do with weakness emanating from ServiceNow than anything having to do with the companies themselves," he said.
The pattern has emerged elsewhere in technology. Cramer pointed to Alphabet's disappointing earnings on Wednesday evening, which dragged down Microsoft despite the software giant's strong quarterly results. Similarly, Samsung's conservative outlook Thursday pressured Micron shares, "even as Micron's book of high bandwidth memory is much stronger than Samsung's. Another buy."
"Some of these guilty verdicts are downright absurd," he said.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Microsoft is winning the AI spending battle — and Alphabet is paying the price
articles.text:
Mad Money
Jim Cramer says Microsoft is winning the AI spending battle — and Alphabet is paying the price
Key Points
- CNBC’s Jim Cramer said Wall Street has shifted from rewarding aggressive AI spending to favoring companies that demonstrate financial discipline and returns on their investments.
- Cramer said Microsoft’s strong earnings and restrained spending make it a buy, while Alphabet’s disappointing results and mounting AI costs have left him cautious on the stock.
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Thursday that the market's reaction to Microsoft and Alphabet's latest earnings underscores a major shift in how Wall Street evaluates the enormous costs of the artificial intelligence boom. Investors who once rewarded tech giants for aggressively building AI infrastructure are now prioritizing financial discipline and returns on those investments. Earlier this year, Microsoft's relatively restrained spending raised concerns that it could fall behind competitors, while Alphabet was rewarded for pouring money into data centers and custom chips. But Cramer said the companies' earnings Wednesday night showed how dramatically investors' priorities have changed. "I think the stock of Microsoft, with all of its discipline, is now set to soar, while the stock of Alphabet won't rally," the " Mad Money " host said. "Too much baggage for Alphabet. No discipline. No sense of what it's supposed to be doing." Cramer's Charitable Trust , the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club, owns shares of both Alphabet and Microsoft. On Wednesday night, Microsoft topped earnings and revenue expectations , with revenue for its Azure cloud business growing 48% from a year earlier. Capital expenditures and finance leases of $45.2 billion also came in below Wall Street's forecasts. Cramer praised Microsoft's ability to deliver strong cloud growth while remaining free-cash-flow positive. He also highlighted the success of Copilot, its AI assistant for businesses, which "started slow, but it is becoming a screaming success." "The combination of a shrewd CEO in Satya Nadella and a tight-fisted, canny CFO in Amy Hood resulted in a quarter that will have Microsoft pull away from the crowd," Cramer said. "They run it like a business, not a science project," he added. Alphabet, meanwhile, disappointed investors. Shares plunged in Thursday's session after the Google parent missed earnings and revenue expectations , with both Search and YouTube ad revenue falling short of estimates. Although Google Cloud revenue more than doubled, that strength wasn't enough to offset concerns about its core businesses. He argued that Alphabet's massive AI investments have become harder to justify as its cash generation deteriorates. The company expects capital expenditures of $195 billion to $205 billion this year, while free cash flow turned negative for the second consecutive quarter. He also warned that Alphabet's remaining $27.6 billion in authorized stock sales could weigh on shares. "I don't want to buy more Alphabet," Cramer said. "Today was the worst day the stock ever had, but I have to wait a little bit. Let the analysts cut numbers, see where it trades, find out the right multiple." "Microsoft?
